# P0 — Start here

# What is Qefro?

Source: https://docs.qefro.com/docs/introduction/overview/

> Qefro is an AI Workspace platform with Customer/Employee assistants, metadata Marketplace Apps executed by Runtime, and secure Business Tools.

Qefro is an **AI Workspace platform** for organizations. You configure knowledge,
permissions, and tools once, then ship three product surfaces:

- **Assistants** — **Customer AI** (website widget, WhatsApp) and **Employee AI**
  (branded Internal Portal), grounded in workspace knowledge with citations
- **Marketplace Apps** — metadata packages (`qefro app init`) published to
  **Marketplace**, installed per workspace, executed by **Qefro Runtime**
  (UI, entities, storage, Business Flows, events, CRM, Automation)
- **Secure actions** — **Business Tools** (REST / OpenAPI / Backend SDK webhook)
  for connecting **external** ERP / POS / CRM systems over `/qefro`

Assistants answer questions and run **Business Actions**. Marketplace Apps
own vertical metadata (reservations, listings, bookings) while the platform
owns Customer Hub (People), campaigns, organization workflows, and Runtime
execution. The SDK is for **external** systems, not for building Marketplace
Apps.

**Configure once. Deploy everywhere.** Workspaces isolate knowledge and tools.
Install apps from Marketplace without forking per tenant. Events, chat, and
schedules enter the same Runtime.

## Who this documentation is for

| Audience | Focus | Start here |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Operators & admins | Run workspaces, install apps, People | [Operate → Getting started](/docs/user/getting-started) |
| App builders | Ship metadata Marketplace Apps | [Build apps → First app](/docs/solutions/build-your-first-app) |
| Integrators | Connect REST / OpenAPI / SDK to existing systems | [Build apps → Connect systems](/docs/business-tools) |
| Spec lookup | APIs, schemas, security | [Reference](/docs/reference/overview) |

**Orientation**

# Qefro Architecture

Source: https://docs.qefro.com/docs/architecture/overview/

> Platform architecture: Admin Console, Qefro Runtime, FlowRunner, Metadata Marketplace Apps, Channels, External Integrations, and Security Boundaries.

This document defines the canonical architecture of Qefro as of October 2026: **the system topology, execution planes, trust boundaries, and component ownership.**

---

## 1. High-Level Canonical Architecture

Qefro coordinates AI Workspaces, declarative Marketplace Apps, and external enterprise systems through a single multi-tenant runtime:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  subgraph PLATFORM["QEFRO PLATFORM"]
    direction TB
    WS["AI Workspaces\n(Teams, Knowledge, Context)"]
    MKT["Marketplace\n(Catalog Registry & Signing)"]
    EXT["External Systems\n(Integration Layer)"]
  end

  MKT -->|"Packages\n(manifest, entities, flows, ui)"| META["Metadata Apps"]
  META -->|"Installed Package"| RT["Qefro Runtime"]
  WS -->|"Conversation & Config"| RT

  subgraph RUNTIME["Qefro Runtime Engine"]
    direction TB
    RAG["Hybrid RAG\n(Zvec Vector + BM25)"]
    FR["FlowRunner\n(State Machine Orchestrator)"]
    BUS["Event Bus\n(PostgreSQL + Idempotency)"]
    ACT["Runtime Actions\n(Entity CRUD + HTTP Executor)"]
  end

  RT --> RAG
  RT --> FR
  RT --> BUS
  RT --> ACT

  EXT -->|"REST / OpenAPI / SDK Connection"| CONN["External Connectors"]
  CONN --> EXT_SYS["Customer ERP / CRM / POS / Backends\n(Focus ERP, ERPNext, Odoo, SAP, Custom)"]
```

---

## 2. Two Distinct Application & Integration Models

The platform enforces a strict architectural boundary between native business applications and external integrations. They are **not** hosting variants of the same application model:

```text
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ MODEL A: METADATA MARKETPLACE APP                                                │
│                                                                                  │
│   Developer ──▶ App Generator ──▶ Metadata Package ──▶ Marketplace Registry      │
│                                                              │                   │
│                                                       Workspace Install          │
│                                                              ▼                   │
│                                                        Qefro Runtime             │
│                                              (Entities · Flows · UI · Events)    │
│                                                                                  │
│   • No application server or Docker container required                           │
│   • Executed natively by Qefro Runtime                                           │
│   • Managed storage triple-isolated (tenant_id / workspace_id / installation_id) │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ MODEL B: EXTERNAL SYSTEM INTEGRATION                                             │
│                                                                                  │
│   Qefro Runtime (FlowRunner) ──▶ REST / OpenAPI / SDK Connection ──▶ Ext Backend │
│                                                                      (ERP / POS) │
│                                                                                  │
│   • Connects to existing external systems of record                              │
│   • Runs on customer or third-party infrastructure                               │
│   • Backend SDK communicates over HMAC-signed webhooks (`/qefro`)                │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

---

## 3. Platform Layers and Responsibilities

| Layer | Primary Responsibilities | What It Does NOT Do |
|---|---|---|
| **Admin Console** (`app.qefro.com`) | Tenant onboarding, AI Workspace configuration, team RBAC, knowledge document ingestion, Marketplace browsing and installation. | Never executes live chat turns or business workflows directly. |
| **Qefro Runtime** (`ai-customer-support`) | Chat orchestration, RAG context construction, candidate tool selection, action authority validation, FlowRunner step execution, entity mutations, and event emission. | Does not run arbitrary customer code or host third-party application servers. |
| **Marketplace Registry & Installer** | Package validation, Ed25519 cryptographic signing, catalog discovery, workspace installation, version management, and UI bundle storage. | Never runs application logic; it manages package distributions. |
| **FlowRunner** | Deterministic multi-step business flow state machine. Handles step advancement, parameter resolution, conditions, delays, external waits, and resumes. | Does not allow unauthenticated or unauthorized action execution. |
| **Channels** | Inbound and outbound message processing for Website Widget, WhatsApp Cloud API, Instagram Messaging API, and authenticated REST Chat APIs. | Never bypasses workspace tenancy or runtime action authorization. |
| **External SDK Connections** | Signed HTTPS webhook bridge (`/qefro`) allowing Qefro to invoke actions in customer-hosted backends (e.g. Focus ERP, Yaaz, custom ERPs). | Cannot invoke Marketplace entity operations or access Qefro runtime storage. |
| **Connectors (Shared Pool)** | Shared, stateless webhook receivers normalizing upstream events (e.g., Stripe, Shopify, Razorpay) into standard Qefro event envelopes. | Connectors never run workflow logic; they only emit events onto the bus. |

---

## 4. Execution Pipeline & Action Authority

Qefro enforces the principle that **the model is never the authority boundary**.

When an end user interacts with Qefro via chat or when an event triggers an automation, the runtime executes a four-tier pipeline:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  UserMsg["User Message / Inbound Event"] --> Tier1["1. Deterministic Pattern Match\n(Exact string match, bypasses LLM)"]
  Tier1 -->|Miss| Tier2["2. Fast Router\n(Semantic embedding similarity)"]
  Tier2 -->|Miss| Tier3["3. FlowRunner\n(Active or candidate Business Flow)"]
  Tier3 -->|Miss| Tier4["4. Agent LLM Reasoning\n(Model proposes candidate actions)"]

  Tier3 --> AuthCheck["Runtime Action Authority Check"]
  Tier4 --> AuthCheck

  subgraph SECURITY_ENFORCEMENT["Authority Enforcement"]
    direction TB
    Strip["Strip Forbidden Authority Keys\n(tenant_id, workspace_id, person_id, created_by)"]
    RBAC["App & Org RBAC Check\n(Role & Capability verification)"]
    Inject["Identity Injection\n(Inject authenticated Person from Customer Hub)"]
  end

  AuthCheck --> Strip --> RBAC --> Inject --> Exec["Actual Execution\n(RuntimeAdapter: entity.* CRUD | HTTP Executor | SDK)"]
```

1. **Model Proposes, Runtime Authorizes:** The LLM produces candidate actions and parameter values.
2. **Authority Stripping:** The runtime unconditionally strips protected parameters (`tenant_id`, `workspace_id`, `installation_id`, `person_id`, etc.) from untrusted inputs.
3. **RBAC & Capability Verification:** The runtime validates that the workspace and caller have the required capability and role before execution.
4. **Identity Injection:** Identity fields (such as `person_id`) are injected server-side from the authenticated session, never from model text.
5. **Execution:** Only validated actions reach the `RuntimeAdapter` (for Marketplace entity operations) or `SDKAdapter` (for external systems).

---

## 5. FlowRunner: Single Canonical Workflow Engine

All workflows in Qefro execute through **FlowRunner**, whether triggered by conversational intent, business events, cron schedules, or incoming webhooks.

There is **no secondary workflow engine**:

- Connectors do **not** run workflows; they emit events.
- Marketplace Apps define flows as metadata (`workflows/*.yaml`), which compile into FlowRunner definitions.
- FlowRunner manages step execution, state transitions, variables, retries, and waiting states (user input, file uploads, human approvals, or identity challenges).

See **[FlowRunner Architecture](/docs/developer/concepts/flows)** and **[Define Business Flows](/docs/guides/define-business-flows)** for details.

---

## 6. Tenancy & Isolation Hierarchy

Qefro guarantees strict multi-tenant isolation at every layer:

```text
Organization (Tenant)
  └── Teams & Org RBAC (Owner / Admin / Member)
        └── AI Workspaces
              ├── Knowledge Base & RAG Index (Isolated Vector Collection)
              ├── Channel Connections (Widget, WhatsApp, Instagram)
              ├── Customer Hub (People records scoped to tenant)
              └── Marketplace App Installations
                    ├── Metadata Bundle (manifest, entities, flows, ui)
                    ├── Installation Settings (operating configs)
                    └── Runtime Managed Storage (triple-keyed)
```

### Triple-Keyed Data Isolation

Every record stored by Marketplace Apps is triple-keyed in runtime storage:

```text
Key = (tenant_id, workspace_id, installation_id)
```

No query can execute without all three keys present in the authenticated `StorageContext`. Data from one installation or workspace can never bleed into another.

---

## 7. What Qefro Deliberately Is Not

To maintain architectural clarity, Qefro explicitly avoids these legacy or mismatched patterns:

- **Not an Application Container Host:** Qefro does not run customer Docker containers or deploy customer application code in the cloud. Marketplace Apps are pure declarative metadata.
- **Not a Replacement for Enterprise ERPs:** Qefro does not replace SAP, NetSuite, or Focus ERP. It connects to them as the intelligent reasoning and action layer via SDK Connections and REST APIs.
- **Not a Generic Graph Framework:** Qefro does not require developers to hand-code Python LangGraph loops or maintain ad-hoc agent states. Business flows are declarative, auditable, and state-machine backed.

---

# Qefro vs n8n

Source: https://docs.qefro.com/docs/compare/n8n-vs-qefro/

> How Qefro differs from n8n-style workflow automation — AI Workspaces, channels, and a product Runtime vs general-purpose automation.

Teams often ask whether Qefro replaces **n8n** (or Make, Zapier, Windmill). Short answer: **usually no — different jobs.** n8n is a general automation canvas. Qefro is an **AI Workspace platform** with grounded chat, Business Tools, and FlowRunner for customer/employee processes.

## Short definition (citation-ready)

> **n8n** optimizes for flexible, developer-operated workflow automation across hundreds of apps. **Qefro** optimizes for multi-tenant AI Workspaces — hybrid RAG assistants, channel delivery, authorized tools, and business flows with approvals — with connectors that only emit events into one Runtime.

## Capability matrix

## Architecture difference

```mermaid
flowchart TB
  subgraph n8nWorld[n8n-style]
    T1[Trigger] --> N1[Node]
    N1 --> N2[Node]
    N2 --> N3[Node]
  end

  subgraph QefroWorld[Qefro]
    Ch[Channels / chat] --> RT[Runtime]
    Ev[Connectors emit] --> Bus[Event bus]
    Bus --> FR[FlowRunner]
    RT --> RAG[RAG]
    RT --> FR
    FR --> Tools[Tools / SDK]
    Admin[Admin Console] -.-> RT
  end
```

- **n8n:** the workflow *is* the product surface. You own hosting, auth UX, chat UI, and RAG if you need them.
- **Qefro:** the **Workspace + Runtime** are the product. Flows are one execution path alongside chat and knowledge — not a generic node marketplace.

## When to choose which

| Situation | Lean toward |
| --- | --- |
| Sync Shopify → Sheets → Slack with no AI product | n8n-class |
| Customer-facing AI with citations + WhatsApp | Qefro |
| Employee AI portal with RBAC | Qefro |
| Heavy multi-app back-office glue | n8n-class |
| AI that must call your APIs with audit + approvals | Qefro |
| Both AI support product and messy SaaS glue | **Often both** |

## Typical coexistence

1. **n8n** handles back-office integrations (billing exports, internal alerts, data sync).
2. **Qefro** owns customer/employee AI, knowledge, and guided business processes.
3. Bridge options:
   - n8n HTTP node → Qefro [org events API](/docs/guides/event-driven-triggers)
   - Qefro Business Tool → internal API that n8n also uses
   - Shared system of record (Shopify, Odoo, Postgres)

## What confuses people

| Confusion | Reality |
| --- | --- |
| “Qefro is just another workflow tool” | Flows are **business process + AI** primitives; RAG and channels are first-class |
| “n8n already has AI nodes” | Useful for experiments; not a multi-tenant workspace product with Admin Console and widget |
| “Connectors run the workflow” | In Qefro, connectors **emit**; FlowRunner executes |

# Qefro vs LangGraph

Source: https://docs.qefro.com/docs/compare/langgraph-vs-qefro/

> How Qefro differs from LangGraph-style agent frameworks — productized Runtime and Admin Console vs library-level graph control.

**LangGraph** (and similar agent frameworks) give engineers fine-grained control over graph state machines for LLM agents. **Qefro** is a multi-tenant **product**: Admin Console, Hybrid RAG, channels, Business Tools, FlowRunner, and org security — so teams ship Customer AI and Employee AI without building the platform.

## Short definition (citation-ready)

> **LangGraph** is a library for composing stateful agent graphs in your own runtime. **Qefro** is an AI Workspace platform: operators configure knowledge and flows; a managed Runtime executes chat, tools, events, approvals, and challenges across channels.

## Capability matrix

## Control plane difference

| Concern | LangGraph-class | Qefro |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Prompt / graph changes | Deploy code | Often Console + version Accept for flows |
| Document updates | Your ingestion jobs | Knowledge upload / crawl in product |
| Who can approve refunds | Your admin UI | Flow Runs / approvals in product |
| Observability | Your APM + traces | Flow runs, tool logs, platform metrics |
| Customer identity | Your session model | Channel sessions + Customer Hub |

## When LangGraph is the better fit

- You are building a **bespoke agent product** and need exotic graph topologies, custom memory policies, or research-grade control.
- You already own multi-tenant auth, document pipelines, widget, WhatsApp, and ops tooling.
- The “UI” is your application, not an Admin Console for business operators.

## When Qefro is the better fit

- You need **Customer AI / Employee AI** with grounded answers quickly.
- Business users must manage knowledge, channels, and some process configuration.
- Tools must call **your** backends with clear auth, challenges, and audit.
- You want connectors to **emit events** into a shared orchestration model — not host a second agent runtime per integration.

## Coexistence patterns

Qefro does not ban frameworks in **your** Backend SDK:

1. **Qefro owns the channel and workspace** — chat, RAG, flow steps that call tools.
2. **A tool handler** may call an internal service that uses LangGraph (or any agent stack) for a specialized sub-task.
3. Return a structured tool result; Qefro continues the conversation or flow.

```text
Widget → Qefro Runtime → tool.invoke → your SDK
                              └── optional internal LangGraph service
```

Do **not** run a second public orchestrator that bypasses workspace isolation and audit unless you intentionally accept that complexity.

## Mental model

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  subgraph Framework[LangGraph-class]
    Code[Your code] --> Graph[Agent graph]
    Graph --> Tools1[Tools you wire]
  end

  subgraph Product[Qefro]
    Console[Admin Console] --> RT[Runtime]
    RT --> Flows[FlowRunner]
    RT --> RAG[RAG]
    Flows --> SDK[Your Backend SDK]
  end
```

Frameworks maximize **graph freedom**. Qefro maximizes **product completeness** for AI Workspaces.

# Core Concepts

Source: https://docs.qefro.com/docs/introduction/concepts/

> Core architectural concepts of Qefro — AI Workspaces, Metadata Marketplace Apps, Qefro Runtime, FlowRunner, External SDK Connections, and Customer Hub.

Understanding Qefro begins with five fundamental architectural concepts:

---

## 1. AI Workspaces & Tenancy

| Concept | Summary | Read more |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Organization (Tenant)** | Top-level customer boundary. Encapsulates teams, billing, and global Customer Hub People. | [Organizations](/docs/platform/organizations) |
| **AI Workspace** | Isolated operational context. Owns dedicated knowledge collections, channel connections, tools, and Marketplace app installations. | [What is an AI Workspace?](/docs/concepts/what-is-an-ai-workspace) |
| **Customer AI vs Employee AI** | Customer-facing channels (Website Widget, WhatsApp, Instagram) vs Employee-facing Internal Portal. | [Customer vs Employee](/docs/concepts/customer-ai-vs-employee-ai) |
| **Hybrid RAG** | Document grounding combining dense semantic vectors (Zvec) and BM25 sparse keyword ranking with strict citations. | [Hybrid RAG](/docs/concepts/hybrid-rag) |
| **RBAC** | Organization-level roles (Owner, Admin, Member) and installation-level app RBAC. | [RBAC](/docs/platform/rbac) |

---

## 2. Marketplace Apps vs External System Integrations

Qefro enforces two distinct execution paradigms:

| Dimension | Metadata Marketplace App | External System Integration |
|---|---|---|
| **Primary Role** | Domain applications owned and executed by Qefro (Hospitality, Clinic, Real Estate, Appointments). | Connecting existing systems of record (Focus ERP, ERPNext, Odoo, custom backends). |
| **Format** | Declarative metadata package (`manifest.yaml`, `entities/`, `workflows/`, `ui/`, `events/`). | Signed HTTPS webhook bridge or REST/OpenAPI tool definitions. |
| **Hosting & Execution** | **`hosting: runtime`** — executed natively by **Qefro Runtime**. No app server or Docker container. | Customer/third-party infrastructure running the Qefro Backend SDK (`POST /qefro`) or REST API. |
| **Data Plane** | Managed runtime storage triple-keyed to `(tenant_id, workspace_id, installation_id)`. | External database managed by the customer's ERP or backend. |
| **Developer Journey** | `qefro app init` ➔ metadata authoring ➔ `validate` ➔ `package` ➔ `publish`. | Implement SDK handlers ➔ run service ➔ register SDK Connection in Workspace. |

Learn more: **[Runtime vs SDK](/docs/solutions/runtime-vs-sdk)** · **[Integration Decision Guide](/docs/developer/integration-models)**.

---

## 3. Qefro Runtime & FlowRunner

| Concept | Summary | Read more |
|---|---|---|
| **Qefro Runtime** | The unified engine executing chat turns, RAG retrieval, FlowRunner state transitions, entity CRUD, and event dispatch. | [Runtime Architecture](/docs/developer/concepts/runtime) |
| **FlowRunner** | Deterministic multi-step business workflow engine. Orchestrates steps (ask, tool, message, condition, approval, challenge). | [FlowRunner](/docs/developer/concepts/flows) |
| **Runtime Actions** | Secure execution capabilities (`entity.<id>.create`, `execution: runtime` or HTTP calls). Governed by runtime authority checks. | [Business Actions](/docs/concepts/business-actions) |
| **Action Authority** | Independent security boundary. Unconditionally strips caller authority parameters and verifies permissions before execution. | [AI Agent Security](/docs/concepts/ai-agent-security) |
| **Business Events** | Standardized JSON envelopes emitted onto the PostgreSQL event bus triggering automations and flows. | [Events](/docs/developer/concepts/events) |

---

## 4. Platform Hubs & Capabilities

| Capability | Summary | Read more |
|---|---|---|
| **Customer Hub (People)** | Tenant-wide customer identity repository. Cross-channel person identity (`whatsapp:{phone}`, `instagram:{id}`, email). | [People Overview](/docs/user/people/overview) · [Customer Hub](/docs/solutions/customer-hub) |
| **Automation** | Event-driven rules (`event ➔ condition ➔ action`) for tag assignment, follow-ups, and notifications. | [Event-Driven Triggers](/docs/guides/event-driven-triggers) |
| **Global Tax Engine** | Configurable tax determination and calculation rules for orders, invoices, and bookings across jurisdictions. | [Tax Engine](/docs/solutions/tax-engine) |
| **Marketplace Registry** | Cryptographically signed catalog where verified apps are published and installed into workspaces. | [Marketplace](/docs/solutions/marketplace) |

---

## 5. Security & Trust Principles

1. **The model is not the authority boundary:** LLMs propose candidate parameters; the runtime strictly validates, strips forbidden authority keys, and authorizes actions.
2. **Triple-keyed storage isolation:** Every Marketplace record requires `(tenant_id, workspace_id, installation_id)`.
3. **Encrypted secrets at rest:** All API tokens and integration credentials are encrypted with AES-256-GCM.
4. **HMAC Webhook Signatures:** Platform-to-SDK calls and Meta webhooks require cryptographic signature verification.

---

# User Guide — Getting Started

Source: https://docs.qefro.com/docs/user/getting-started/

> Create your organization, first AI Workspace, upload knowledge, and test chat in the Admin Console.

# Getting Started (User Guide)

This path is for **operators and admins** using [app.qefro.com](https://app.qefro.com) — no backend code required.

## Outcome

- Organization ready with at least one Owner
- One AI Workspace with documents indexed
- Test chat returns cited answers
- Optional: website widget or WhatsApp bound to the workspace

## Steps

1. **Sign up / sign in** at [app.qefro.com](https://app.qefro.com).
2. **Create an AI Workspace** (e.g. Support) — [Workspaces](/docs/user/workspaces/overview).
3. **Upload knowledge** (PDF, DOCX, Markdown, crawl) — [Knowledge Base](/docs/user/knowledge-base/overview).
4. **Test in Admin Console chat** until citations look correct — [Quick Start](/docs/getting-started/quick-start).
5. **Invite teammates** and set roles — [Administration](/docs/user/administration/overview).
6. **Connect a channel** — [Website widget](/docs/user/channels/website-widget) or [WhatsApp](/docs/user/channels/whatsapp).
7. **Add Business Tools** (optional) when you need actions, not only answers — [Developer Guide](/docs/developer/quick-start) or ask engineering to register the Backend SDK.

Need order status, refunds, or Shopify events? That is a **developer + integrations** path. Start with [Business Tools](/docs/business-tools) and [Integrations](/docs/integrations/overview).

# User Guide (what to do)

# How to create an AI agent

Source: https://docs.qefro.com/docs/user/how-to/create-ai-agent/

> Create an AI Workspace agent for customers or employees — knowledge, personality, and channels.

In Qefro, an “AI agent” is delivered as an **AI Workspace** configuration: knowledge, instructions, tools, and channels — not a separate unmanaged chatbot silo.

## Choose the agent type

| Type | Audience | Typical channel |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Customer AI** | Your customers | Website widget, WhatsApp |
| **Employee AI** | Internal staff | Internal Portal |

See [Customer AI](/docs/platform/customer-ai) and [Employee AI](/docs/platform/employee-ai).

## Steps

1. Sign in at [app.qefro.com](https://app.qefro.com).
2. **Create an AI Workspace** with a clear name (Support, HR, IT, Sales).
3. **Upload knowledge** — policies, product docs, SOPs. Wait until indexing succeeds.
4. Set **instructions / personality** for the workspace (tone, handoff rules, languages).
5. **Test in Console chat** — require citations; fix missing docs when answers are weak.
6. **Invite teammates** and assign workspace access — [Administration](/docs/user/administration/overview).
7. **Publish a channel**:
   - Customers → [Website widget](/docs/user/channels/website-widget) and/or [Configure WhatsApp](/docs/user/how-to/configure-whatsapp)
   - Employees → Internal Portal branding and access
8. Optional: ask engineering for **Business Tools** when the agent must take actions (orders, tickets).

One workspace = one knowledge and tool boundary. Prefer **separate workspaces** over one mega-bot when teams or data must not mix.

## Workflow

## Related topics

# How to configure WhatsApp

Source: https://docs.qefro.com/docs/user/how-to/configure-whatsapp/

> Connect WhatsApp as a Customer AI channel for an AI Workspace.

**Goal:** Customers message your business on WhatsApp and reach the same grounded Customer AI as your website widget.

## Prerequisites

- Plan that includes WhatsApp (typically **Growth+** — confirm on your billing page)
- Owner or Admin role
- Meta / WhatsApp Business assets ready (Business portfolio, WABA, phone number) — engineering or a partner may complete Meta-side setup
- Target **AI Workspace** with indexed knowledge

## Steps (operator)

1. Open [app.qefro.com](https://app.qefro.com) → **Channels** / WhatsApp settings (wording may vary slightly by release).
2. Select the **AI Workspace** that should answer WhatsApp traffic.
3. Complete provider connection (embedded signup or admin fields your org uses).
4. Confirm the **phone number** shows as connected / quality pending as applicable.
5. Send a test message from a personal WhatsApp to the business number.
6. In **Conversations**, open the thread and verify:
   - Reply is grounded (citations / correct policy)
   - Handoff behavior matches your instructions
7. Optional: enable Business Tools so WhatsApp users can check orders (same tools as widget).

WhatsApp template / marketing outbound rules are governed by Meta. Qefro focuses on the **AI session** once the customer is in a supported messaging context. Follow Meta policy for opt-in and templates.

## Workflow

## Troubleshooting

| Symptom | What to check |
| --- | --- |
| No reply | Number bound? Workspace correct? API healthy? |
| Wrong knowledge | Different workspace than widget — align bindings |
| Tools fail | Same as web: tool auth / Customer Provider — ask engineering |

Deep technical guide: [Deploy WhatsApp AI](/docs/guides/deploy-whatsapp-ai). Platform overview: [WhatsApp](/docs/platform/whatsapp).

# How to connect Shopify

Source: https://docs.qefro.com/docs/user/how-to/connect-shopify/

> Operator steps to connect Shopify so Qefro can use commerce data and events for your AI Workspace.

**Goal:** Link your Shopify store so support or commerce assistants can use order/catalog context and event-driven CRM automations.

## Who does what

| Role | Tasks |
| --- | --- |
| **You (admin)** | Install the Shopify Marketplace app, enter **your** Shopify app client ID and secret, shop domain, then **Connect Shopify** |
| **Engineering** | Qefro Runtime HTTPS callback (`PUBLIC_API_URL`) — not Shopify app credentials |

Qefro Marketplace Shopify is **metadata + generic Runtime HTTP**. There is no
Shopify SDK in the app package. Tools run:

`Shopify metadata → FlowRunner → RuntimeAdapter → Generic HTTP Executor → Shopify Admin API`

SDK connections stay for Focus ERP / Yaaz only.

## What you need

- Owner or Admin on the Qefro organization
- Shopify store admin access
- A target **AI Workspace** (e.g. Support or Commerce)
- The **Shopify** Marketplace app installed on that workspace
- A Shopify Partner app (client ID and secret) for **this** workspace

## Steps (operator)

1. Open [app.qefro.com](https://app.qefro.com) → your organization.
2. Open the **AI Workspace** that should own commerce answers and tools.
3. Open **Tools → Marketplace app** and install **Shopify** if it is not already installed.
4. Under **Store connection**, enter:
   - `your-store.myshopify.com`
   - Shopify app **client ID** and **secret** from Partners (this workspace only — Qefro does not use a shared app secret)
   - Click **Connect**.
5. Approve the requested scopes in Shopify (products, customers, orders — from the app metadata).
6. After redirect, the card shows **Connected**. Tokens are never shown in the UI.
7. Confirm **knowledge** is ready for policies (shipping, returns) — [Knowledge Base](/docs/user/knowledge-base/overview).
8. From Admin Console chat, try:
   - “List all orders” (shop-wide, **staff only**)
   - “Where is order 1001?”
   - “What is your return window?” (should cite knowledge, not invent policy)
9. Optional: enable **website widget** or **WhatsApp** on the same workspace — [Channels](/docs/user/channels/overview). On WhatsApp, “show my recent orders” uses **that customer’s** Hub email (OTP-verified if missing), not the shop-wide staff list.
10. Optional outcomes: [Order tracking](/docs/solutions/order-tracking), [Abandoned cart](/docs/solutions/abandoned-cart).

**Reconnect** runs OAuth again and replaces credentials. **Disconnect** revokes the token and deletes stored credentials; tools then fail safely until you connect again.

## Workflow

## Events (webhooks)

After Connect, Qefro registers webhooks for the topics declared in the app metadata. Inbound requests hit a **generic Qefro webhook** (`/webhooks/http/shopify`), not a Shopify server in the package.

HMAC is checked on the **raw body** first. The shop domain header selects the workspace — the payload cannot pick a workspace. Topics map to Business Events:

| Shopify topic | Business Event |
| --- | --- |
| `orders/create` | `order.created` |
| `orders/updated` | `order.updated` |
| `orders/cancelled` | `order.cancelled` |
| `customers/create` | `customer.created` |
| `customers/update` | `customer.updated` |

Those events go onto `orchestration_events` and can start **CRM Automation**. People are matched through **Customer Hub** (email/phone/existing mapping). Shopify customer ids are never used as Person IDs.

## Troubleshooting

| Symptom | What to check |
| --- | --- |
| Assistant cannot see orders | Connected? Correct workspace? Scope `read_orders` granted? Protected customer data approved in Partner? |
| WhatsApp shows no orders / asks for email | Person needs a **verified Hub email** matching the Shopify customer. Reply with the email, then the OTP. Shop-wide `list_orders` is staff-only. |
| Customer sees another person's order | Should not happen — ownership is checked after Shopify responds. File a bug if it does. |
| Wrong store data | Confirm which shop is bound to this workspace |
| “Already connected to another workspace” | Disconnect the other workspace first |
| Events not starting flows | Event names + CRM Automation trigger — [Event-driven triggers](/docs/guides/event-driven-triggers) |
| Connect button fails | Client ID/secret for **this** workspace? Shop domain `*.myshopify.com`? Partner redirect URL matches Qefro callback? |

## Related topics

---

# How to track orders

Source: https://docs.qefro.com/docs/user/how-to/track-orders/

> Let customers ask where their order is — knowledge plus order-status tools on your AI Workspace.

**Goal:** Customers ask “Where is my order?” on widget or WhatsApp and get a factual status from **your** commerce system — not a hallucinated ETA.

## What you need

- AI Workspace for Support or Commerce
- Policy docs in knowledge (shipping times, carriers) for non-account questions
- For Shopify: install **Shopify** on the workspace and Connect the store — [Connect Shopify](/docs/user/how-to/connect-shopify)
- Engineering (non-Shopify): an order-status Business Tool or SDK handler
- Customer identity: Hub email (WhatsApp collects and OTP-verifies it when missing)

## Steps (operator)

1. Create or open the workspace — [Create an AI agent](/docs/user/how-to/create-ai-agent).
2. Upload **shipping and delivery FAQs** to knowledge.
3. For Shopify, skip a custom tool: customer WhatsApp “show my recent orders” / “where is my order” uses `list_my_orders` / `get_my_order` with Hub email + ownership. Otherwise ask engineering to register an order status tool — [Order tracking solution](/docs/solutions/order-tracking).
4. In Console test chat (staff), try shop-wide “list all orders” and a sandbox order id.
5. On WhatsApp, confirm the assistant **asks for email + OTP** when the Person has no Hub email, then returns **only that customer’s** orders.
6. Enable the customer channel (widget / WhatsApp).
7. Spot-check **Conversations** in the first days; refine instructions if the model skips the tool.

Order data always comes from **tools** (or events), never from the LLM’s training data. If the tool is down, the assistant should say so — not invent tracking numbers.

## Related topics

# How to add an approval workflow

Source: https://docs.qefro.com/docs/user/how-to/add-approval-workflow/

> Require a supervisor approval step before a Business Flow continues (for example refunds).

**Goal:** A Business Flow pauses until an **Owner or Admin** approves (or rejects) in the Admin Console — for example before a refund tool runs.

## Who does what

| Role | Tasks |
| --- | --- |
| **Engineering** | Declares `.approval()` (or equivalent) in the Backend SDK flow definition and syncs the flow |
| **You (admin)** | Accepts the flow version, monitors Flow Runs, approves or rejects |

## Steps (operator)

1. Agree the business rule with engineering (when to pause, approval prompt text, what happens after approve/reject).
2. Engineering ships the flow with an approval step — [Approvals (developer)](/docs/developer/concepts/approvals).
3. In Admin Console, open **Business Flows** (or SDK flows list) and **Accept** the new version when prompted.
4. Run a **safe test** (staging workspace or test order):
   - Start the flow from chat or a test event
   - Confirm run status becomes **waiting for approval**
5. Open **Flow Runs** / **Approvals** — [Approvals overview](/docs/user/approvals/overview).
6. **Approve** or **reject** with a note if available.
7. Confirm the customer conversation continues (tool ran or rejection message shown).

Only **Owner/Admin** can approve via API-enforced checks. Members can usually view conversations but not clear approval gates.

# Knowledge Base

Source: https://docs.qefro.com/docs/user/knowledge-base/overview/

> Upload and index documents so assistants answer with citations from your content.

Train your assistant by adding **documents** to a workspace. Qefro chunks and indexes them with **hybrid RAG** (lexical + vector) and returns **citations** in answers.

## Common tasks

| Task | Notes |
| --- | --- |
| Upload files | PDF, DOCX, Markdown, TXT |
| Add text / crawl | Console flows for raw text and site crawl |
| Reindex | After content changes |
| Verify quality | Admin chat — check citations and refusals |

Validate retrieval quality in the Admin Console **before** enabling public widget or WhatsApp.

# Approvals

Source: https://docs.qefro.com/docs/user/approvals/overview/

> Human approval gates in Business Flows — review and approve from Flow Runs.

When a Business Flow includes an **`approval`** step, the run pauses until an **Owner or Admin** approves in **Flow Runs**.

Approvals are part of flow execution — not a separate product. Engineers declare <code>approval</code> steps in the Backend SDK; operators act on them in the console.

## Operator steps

1. Open **Business Tools → Flow Runs** (or Approvals queue).
2. Open a run with status **waiting_for_approval**.
3. Review variables / timeline → **Approve** (or cancel the run).
4. The customer receives the next message on their channel (widget or WhatsApp).

## Learn more

- [Run Business Flows — Human approval](/docs/guides/run-business-flows)
- [Define Business Flows](/docs/guides/define-business-flows)
- [Secure Business Actions](/docs/guides/secure-business-actions)

# Developer Guide (how it works)

# Developer Quick Start

Source: https://docs.qefro.com/docs/developer/quick-start/

> Register the Backend SDK, advertise tools and flows, sync into a workspace, and optionally emit events.

Connect **your** ERP / POS / CRM as Business Tools over a signed webhook.
Qefro discovers tools and executes them in the **Runtime** — your process
never runs FlowRunner.

This is **not** how you build a Marketplace App. For Restaurant / Clinic /
Real Estate metadata packages, start at
[Build your first app](/docs/solutions/build-your-first-app).

## Choose your SDK

| Language | Package | Guide |
| --- | --- | --- |
| JavaScript / TypeScript | `@qefro-ai/backend` | [JavaScript SDK](/docs/developer/sdk/javascript) |
| Python | `qefro-backend` | [Python SDK](/docs/developer/sdk/python) |
| Rust | `qefro-backend-sdk` | [Rust SDK](/docs/developer/sdk/rust) |

## Minimal path

1. Install the SDK and set `QEFRO_SIGNING_SECRET`.
2. `app.tool(...)` for each business capability.
3. Optional: `app.flow(...)` for multi-step orchestration (conversation and/or [event triggers](/docs/developer/events/overview)).
4. `app.listen({ path: '/qefro' })` on a public HTTPS URL.
5. Admin Console → **SDK Connections** → create connection → **Test** → **Sync Tools**.
6. Enable tools/flows on a workspace and test from chat or emit an event.

Full walkthrough: <a href="/docs/guides/register-sdk-business-tools">Register SDK Business Tools</a>. Flows: <a href="/docs/guides/define-business-flows">Define</a> · <a href="/docs/guides/run-business-flows">Run</a> · <a href="/docs/guides/event-driven-triggers">Event triggers</a>.

# Integration Models & Decision Guide

Source: https://docs.qefro.com/docs/developer/integration-models/

> Decision guide: when to build a Metadata Marketplace App, when to connect via Backend SDK, and when to import REST/OpenAPI APIs.

Qefro provides three distinct ways to build capabilities and integrate software systems. Choosing the right model depends on **who owns the application and where the system of record lives**:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  Start{"Where does the business logic\nand system of record live?"}

  Start -->|"Qefro should own the application,\nentities, storage, and workflows"| MKT["1. Metadata Marketplace App\n(hosting: runtime)"]
  Start -->|"Existing external system with an\nexisting HTTP API"| REST["2. REST / OpenAPI Tool\n(Declarative HTTP Tools)"]
  Start -->|"Existing complex system of record\nrequiring custom logic or on-prem code"| SDK["3. External SDK Connection\n(Backend SDK over /qefro)"]
```

---

## 1. The Three Models Compared

| Dimension | 1. Marketplace App | 2. REST / OpenAPI Tool | 3. External SDK Connection |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Primary Intent** | Build a domain application native to Qefro. | Call an existing third-party or internal REST API. | Bridge an existing enterprise backend or on-prem ERP. |
| **Execution Engine** | **Qefro Runtime** (FlowRunner + RuntimeAdapter). | **Generic HTTP Executor** in Qefro Runtime. | **External Server** running Qefro Backend SDK. |
| **Data Plane** | Qefro managed storage (triple-keyed). | External system API. | External system database. |
| **Hosting Requirement** | **None** (zero servers or containers). | **None** in Qefro (calls existing API). | Customer or partner infrastructure. |
| **Authentication** | Runtime RBAC & platform identity. | Encrypted API keys, Bearer tokens, Basic auth. | Shared HMAC secret (`X-Qefro-Signature`). |
| **Packaging** | Metadata package (`manifest.yaml`, `entities/`, etc.). | OpenAPI 3.0/3.1 spec or HTTP tool YAML. | NPM/PyPI/Cargo library running in service. |

---

## 2. Model 1: Metadata Marketplace App

### Choose this when
> **You are building a domain application that Qefro can own and operate natively.**

You do not have an existing backend for this business function, or you want a turnkey application that runs across workspaces without infrastructure management.

### Examples
- **Hospitality & Restaurants:** Table management, reservation scheduling, menu catalogs, takeaway ordering.
- **Appointments & Clinics:** Patient intake, doctor scheduling, slot availability, consultations.
- **Real Estate:** Property listings, lead management, viewing appointment booking.
- **Internal Operations:** Equipment checkout, maintenance request tracking, internal approvals.
- **Commerce Extensions:** Catalog management with native entity storage.

### Architecture

```text
Developer ──▶ qefro app init ──▶ Metadata Package ──▶ Publish ──▶ Install ──▶ Qefro Runtime
```

- No server code.
- Declarative entities, workflows, and UI.
- Learn more: **[Marketplace App Development Tutorial](/docs/developer/managed-marketplace-app)** · **[Build Your First App](/docs/solutions/build-your-first-app)**.

---

## 3. Model 2: REST / OpenAPI Integration

### Choose this when
> **The external system already exposes a usable, documented HTTP/REST API.**

You have an existing cloud SaaS product, microservice, or webhook provider with an accessible HTTP endpoint, and you want AI assistants or workflows to call it directly.

### Examples
- Querying weather or flight status APIs.
- Triggering marketing emails via SendGrid or Postmark.
- Creating support tickets in Zendesk or Freshdesk.
- Fetching product catalog data from an existing microservice.

### Architecture

```text
Qefro Runtime ──▶ Encrypted HTTP Call (Bearer/API Key) ──▶ External REST API
```

- Import an OpenAPI 3.0/3.1 specification directly in the Admin Console or define HTTP tool YAML.
- Credentials stored encrypted with AES-256-GCM.
- Learn more: **[Connect REST APIs](/docs/guides/connect-rest-apis)** · **[Import OpenAPI](/docs/guides/import-openapi)**.

---

## 4. Model 3: External SDK Connection

### Choose this when
> **The business already has an established external system of record requiring custom logic, on-prem access, or complex transactions.**

The data cannot or should not be duplicated into Qefro, or requires specialized adapters, proprietary database drivers, or private VPC networking.

### Examples
- **Enterprise ERPs:** Focus ERP, SAP, Microsoft Dynamics, ERPNext, Odoo.
- **Legacy POS Systems:** On-premise retail POS or hospitality point-of-sale servers.
- **Custom Backends:** Internal core banking, insurance claims engines, or proprietary databases.

### Architecture

```text
Customer Infrastructure (ERP / POS / DB)
            │
            ▼
   Custom SDK Backend
    (POST /qefro)
            │
            ▼
      SDKAdapter
            │
            ▼
      Qefro Runtime
```

- Developer implements handlers using `@qefro-ai/backend` (TypeScript), `qefro-backend` (Python), or `qefro-backend-sdk` (Rust).
- Qefro communicates with the backend via signed HTTPS webhooks with HMAC validation.
- Learn more: **[External SDK Connection Guide](/docs/developer/external-sdk-connection)** · **[Backend SDK Reference](/docs/business-tools/backend-sdk)**.

---

## 5. Summary Decision Tree

```text
Are you building a domain application from scratch?
 ├─ YES ──▶ Metadata Marketplace App (hosting: runtime)
 └─ NO  ──▶ Does the system expose a standard REST API?
             ├─ YES ──▶ REST / OpenAPI Tool
             └─ NO  ──▶ External SDK Connection (POST /qefro)
```

---

## Related Documentation

- [Runtime vs SDK Comparison](/docs/solutions/runtime-vs-sdk)
- [Marketplace App Development](/docs/developer/managed-marketplace-app)
- [External SDK Connection](/docs/developer/external-sdk-connection)
- [Connect REST APIs](/docs/guides/connect-rest-apis)

# Marketplace App Development

Source: https://docs.qefro.com/docs/developer/managed-marketplace-app/

> Tutorial: build, validate, package, publish, and install a metadata Marketplace App (hosting: runtime) into Qefro Runtime.

This tutorial guides you through building a complete Qefro Marketplace App as **pure declarative metadata** (`hosting: runtime`), publishing it to the catalog, and executing it within **Qefro Runtime**.

You do **not** write a backend server or `/qefro` process for this path.

---

## 1. Prerequisites

- The `qefro` CLI installed on your system.
- Familiarity with YAML and your business domain's data models.
- Platform administrator credentials (`QEFRO_PUBLISHER_ID` and `QEFRO_SIGNING_KEY_HEX`) if publishing to a production catalog.

---

## 2. Initialize the App

Create a new application metadata structure using the generator:

```bash
qefro app init clinic-pro --name "Clinic Pro"
cd clinic-pro
```

This generates the standard metadata directory layout:

```text
clinic-pro/
├── manifest.yaml          # Package metadata, permissions, channels, events
├── entities/              # Entity schemas for runtime managed storage
│   ├── patient.yaml
│   ├── doctor.yaml
│   └── appointment.yaml
├── workflows/             # Business Flows executed by FlowRunner
│   ├── book-appointment.yaml
│   └── cancel-appointment.yaml
└── ui/                    # Declarative staff portal views
    ├── theme.yaml
    ├── navigation.yaml
    ├── pages.yaml
    ├── layouts.yaml
    ├── widgets.yaml
    └── sources.yaml
```

---

## 3. Define the Manifest

```yaml title="manifest.yaml"
id: clinic-pro-runtime
name: Clinic Pro
version: 0.1.0
hosting: runtime                # Executed natively by Qefro Runtime
description: Clinical operations, patient records, and appointment scheduling.
category: healthcare
tags:
  - clinic
  - medical
  - appointments

channels:
  - widget
  - whatsapp

entities:
  - patient
  - doctor
  - appointment

flows:
  - book-appointment
  - cancel-appointment

events:
  - appointment.created
  - appointment.cancelled

permissions:
  - workflow.execute
  - storage.read
  - storage.write
  - storage.update
  - storage.delete

triggers:
  - id: book_appointment
    workflow: book-appointment
    match:
      intents:
        - book an appointment
        - schedule a visit
        - see a doctor
```

---

## 4. Define Entities (`entities/*.yaml`)

Entities represent your business data models and are persisted in triple-keyed runtime storage:

```yaml title="entities/appointment.yaml"
id: appointment
name: Appointment
allocate_code:
  prefix: APT-
  start: 1001

concurrency: optimistic

availability:
  booking:
    datetime_field: scheduled_at
    duration_minutes: 30
    capacity:
      mode: exclusive
      resource:
        field: doctor_id

fields:
  - name: patient_name
    type: string
    required: true

  - name: doctor_id
    type: relation
    ref_entity: doctor
    required: true

  - name: scheduled_at
    type: datetime
    required: true

  - name: status
    type: enum
    enum_values:
      - scheduled
      - confirmed
      - completed
      - cancelled
    default: scheduled

  - name: person_id
    type: person
    description: "Binds record to Customer Hub Person"
```

---

## 5. Define Workflows (`workflows/*.yaml`)

Workflows execute on FlowRunner using native runtime capabilities:

```yaml title="workflows/book-appointment.yaml"
id: book-appointment
name: Book Appointment
steps:
  - id: ask_doctor
    type: ask
    prompt: "Which doctor would you like to see?"
    choices_from:
      entity: doctor
      filter:
        status: active
      label_field: name
      value_field: id

  - id: check_slots
    type: tool
    tool: entity.appointment.availability
    execution: runtime
    input_map:
      kind: "$literal:slots"
      resource: ask_doctor

  - id: ask_slot
    type: ask
    prompt: "Please select an available appointment time:"
    choices_from:
      variable: check_slots.items
      label_field: label
      value_field: start_at

  - id: create_record
    type: tool
    tool: entity.appointment.create
    execution: runtime
    input_map:
      doctor_id: ask_doctor
      scheduled_at: ask_slot
      status: "$literal:scheduled"

  - id: confirm
    type: complete
    message: "Your appointment has been confirmed with {{ask_doctor}} for {{ask_slot}}. Reference: {{create_record.code}}."
```

---

## 6. Define Staff UI (`ui/*.yaml`)

Define responsive dashboards, tables, and forms without writing frontend code:

```yaml title="ui/pages.yaml"
- id: appointments
  title: Appointments
  layout: table
  source: appointments_source
  columns:
    - field: code
      header: Reference
    - field: patient_name
      header: Patient
    - field: scheduled_at
      header: Time
    - field: status
      header: Status

- id: doctors
  title: Doctors
  layout: table
  source: doctors_source
```

```yaml title="ui/sources.yaml"
- id: appointments_source
  type: entity
  target: appointment

- id: doctors_source
  type: entity
  target: doctor
```

---

## 7. Validate, Package & Publish

```bash
# Validate metadata structure and types
qefro app validate .

# Package and sign the distribution artifact
qefro app package .

# Publish to the global Marketplace catalog (Platform Admin)
qefro app publish .
```

---

## 8. Workspace Installation

Once published, tenant administrators can install the app directly into any AI Workspace:

```bash
qefro app install clinic-pro-runtime --version 0.1.0
```

Upon installation:
1. The metadata package is verified via its Ed25519 signature.
2. The UI bundle is registered for the workspace.
3. Entities are initialized with triple-scoped runtime storage.
4. Workflows are registered with FlowRunner.
5. Channels (Widget, WhatsApp, Instagram) begin routing conversational requests to the new flows.

---

- [Build Your First App Walkthrough](/docs/solutions/build-your-first-app)
- [Entity Schemas & Data Model](/docs/solutions/entity-schema)
- [FlowRunner State Machine](/docs/developer/concepts/flows)
- [Concurrency & Booking Integrity](/docs/solutions/concurrency-and-booking)
- [Publishing to the Registry](/docs/solutions/publishing)
