# External SDK Connection

Source: https://docs.qefro.com/docs/developer/external-sdk-connection/

> Tutorial: build a product & quotation connector, deploy /qefro, register an SDK Connection, and sync tools.

:::info Not a Marketplace App
This tutorial connects an **existing** product catalog / ERP / quotation
system to Qefro. To ship Restaurant, Clinic, or Real Estate on Marketplace
without a backend, use
[Marketplace App Development](./managed-marketplace-app.md) instead.
:::

## Goal

Build a **Product & Quotation** style connector that runs on **your** infrastructure and registers as an org **SDK Connection**.

Reference implementations in the monorepo:

| Repo | Role |
| --- | --- |
| `abm-demo` | Full external sales connector (search, pricing, quotation, org approval) |
| `mock-order-status-sdk` | Minimal order-status webhook for Org Portal smoke tests |

This tutorial follows the ABM / quotation pattern with a smaller surface.

## Prerequisites

- Node.js ≥ 18
- `npm install @qefro-ai/backend`
- Public HTTPS URL (or tunnel) ending at `/qefro`
- Org Portal access to **Business Tools → SDK Connections**

## Architecture

```text
AI Sales Assistant
        ↓
ACS / connector-manager
        ↓  HMAC-signed POST
Your server  POST /qefro
        ↓
Existing ERP / catalog / DB
```

```text
ABM ERP
   ↓
ABM SDK Connector
   ↓
Qefro SDK Connection
   ↓
AI Sales Assistant
   ↓
Product Search → Pricing → Quotation → Organization Approval
```

## Create

Example layout (conceptual — mirror `abm-demo`):

```text
quotation-demo/
├── package.json
├── src/
│   └── index.ts   # or server.js
└── README.md
```

```bash
mkdir quotation-demo && cd quotation-demo
npm init -y
npm install @qefro-ai/backend
```

### Initialize the SDK (actual API)

```javascript
const port = Number(process.env.PORT || 8095);
const signingSecret = process.env.QEFRO_SIGNING_SECRET || 'dev-secret-quotation';

const app = new Qefro({
  signingSecret,
  endpointPath: '/qefro',
});
```

Constructor config (`QefroConfig`):

| Field | Required | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `signingSecret` | Yes | — | Shared with the Org Portal SDK Connection |
| `protocolVersion` | No | `'1'` | Must match platform |
| `maxTimestampSkewSeconds` | No | `300` | Replay window |
| `endpointPath` | No | `'/qefro'` | HTTP path |

## Define tools

Conceptual flow:

```text
AI
 ↓
searchProducts
 ↓
External SDK Application
 ↓
Existing ERP / API / database
 ↓
result
```

Qefro does not need to know how you load products.

```javascript
app.tool(
  'searchProducts',
  {
    description: 'Search the product catalog',
    auth: 'none',
    chat: true,
    input_schema: {
      type: 'object',
      properties: {
        query: { type: 'string' },
        limit: { type: 'number' },
      },
    },
  },
  async (ctx) => {
    const query = String(ctx.parameters.query || '').toLowerCase();
    // Replace with ERP/API call
    const items = []; // filtered catalog
    return { items, query };
  },
);

app.tool(
  'getProduct',
  {
    description: 'Fetch a single product by SKU',
    auth: 'none',
    input_schema: {
      type: 'object',
      required: ['sku'],
      properties: { sku: { type: 'string' } },
    },
  },
  async (ctx) => {
    const sku = String(ctx.parameters.sku || '');
    // ERP lookup…
    return { sku, name: 'Example tile', price: 120 };
  },
);

app.tool(
  'calculateQuote',
  {
    description: 'Calculate line totals for a quotation',
    auth: 'optional',
    input_schema: {
      type: 'object',
      properties: {
        lines: { type: 'array' },
        tier: { type: 'string' },
      },
    },
  },
  async (ctx) => {
    // pricing rules in your system
    return { subtotal: 0, tax: 0, total: 0 };
  },
);

app.tool(
  'createQuotation',
  {
    description: 'Persist a quotation; may require org approval above threshold',
    auth: 'optional',
    input_schema: {
      type: 'object',
      properties: {
        customer_name: { type: 'string' },
        lines: { type: 'array' },
        total: { type: 'number' },
      },
    },
  },
  async (ctx) => {
    // persist in your DB; optionally emit org event via platform APIs
    return { id: 'Q-1001', status: 'pending' };
  },
);
```

Optional organization metadata (opaque ids — no `app.` prefix), as in `abm-demo` / Restaurant Pro:

```javascript
app.organization({
  version: 1,
  events: [{ id: 'purchase_requested', label: 'Purchase requested' }],
  actions: [
    { id: 'approve_purchase', label: 'Approve purchase' },
    { id: 'continue_purchase', label: 'Continue purchase' },
  ],
  tasks: [{ id: 'quotation_approval', label: 'Quotation approval', priority: 'high' }],
});
```

## Run

```bash
export QEFRO_SIGNING_SECRET=dev-secret-quotation
export PORT=8095
node src/index.js
# → http://127.0.0.1:8095/qefro
```

`app.listen({ port })` binds `POST` on `endpointPath` only. Other methods/paths return `404` `{ error: 'not_found' }`.

## What `/qefro` receives

Signed JSON body (see [qefro-protocol.md](./qefro-protocol.md)):

```json
{
  "protocol_version": "1",
  "request_id": "…",
  "type": "tool.invoke",
  "organization_id": "…",
  "conversation_id": "…",
  "channel": "whatsapp",
  "identity": {},
  "tool": "searchProducts",
  "parameters": { "query": "flooring tiles" }
}
```

Headers (ACS / connector-manager):

| Header | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `x-qefro-signature` / `X-Qefro-Signature` | `v1={hex}` HMAC |
| `x-qefro-timestamp` | Unix seconds |
| `x-qefro-protocol` | `"1"` |
| `x-qefro-trace-id` | Correlation (when forwarded) |
| `x-qefro-tenant-id` / `x-qefro-workspace-id` | Tenancy (connector-manager path) |

Success tool response: `{ "type": "result", "output": { … } }`.

Errors: `{ "type": "error", "code": "…", "message": "…" }` — see [troubleshooting.md](./troubleshooting.md).

## Create an SDK Connection (Org Portal)

**Confirmed UI:** Org Portal page **SDK Connections** (under **Business Tools**). Route `/app/organization/sdk-connections` redirects to `/app/business-tools`. Product copy may say “Admin Console”; the implemented UI is the portal (`OrganizationAuthentication.tsx`). No SDK Connections UI was found in `ai-customer-support-admin`.

```text
Org Portal
    ↓
Business Tools
    ↓
SDK Connections
    ↓
Add Connection
```

| Field (UI) | API field | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Name | `name` | Required; unique per tenant |
| Webhook URL | `webhook_url` | Your public `/qefro` URL |
| Signing Secret | `signing_secret` | Optional on create — omitted → platform generates |
| Enabled | `enabled` | Defaults to **false** if omitted on create |

Then:

1. **Test Connection** → platform sends `ping`, expects `pong` (status → `healthy` / `degraded`)
2. Select a **workspace** on Business Tools
3. **Sync Tools** → prefer `capabilities.list` ( `tools.list` is legacy); with workspace selected, auto-registers Business Tools (`auto_register`)

REST (ACS; portal client prefixes with the API base):

- `GET/POST /api/v1/org/sdk-connections`
- `PATCH/DELETE /api/v1/org/sdk-connections/{id}`
- `POST /api/v1/org/sdk-connections/{id}/test`
- `POST /api/v1/org/sdk-connections/{id}/sync-tools`
- `GET /api/v1/org/sdk-connections/{id}/flows`

Create requires org admin (+ premium gate on create). Plaintext signing secret is returned only on create/update; list responses expose `has_secret`, not the secret.

```text
Qefro
   ↓
SDK connection
   ↓
External HTTPS endpoint
   ↓
/qefro
```

## Authentication

Shared **connection signing secret**. Platform signs every request:

```text
payload = "v1:{timestamp}:{raw_body}"
signature = "v1=" + hex(HMAC_SHA256(secret, payload))
```

SDK verifies with default **300s** skew. See [authentication.md](./authentication.md).

Rotate: update connection with a new `signing_secret` (API treats empty as generate-new) and redeploy your process with the same value.

## External ownership

You control infrastructure, source, deployment, database, secrets, APIs, availability, scaling, monitoring.

Qefro controls connection routing, HMAC, tenant/workspace routing, AI, workflows, platform capabilities.

**Do not**: attempt to wrap an external ERP system as a Marketplace App; keep it cleanly as an SDK Connection.

## Production considerations

- Prefer HTTPS; ACS validates URL safety (SSRF protections).
- Keep secret out of git; show once on create if platform-generated.
- Monitor `/qefro` latency (ACS timeout ~30s; connector-manager default 30s with retries).
- For org approval actions, keep manager tools off customer chat (`chat: false` on tools).

## Troubleshoot

| Symptom | Check |
| --- | --- |
| Test Connection fails | URL reachable? Path exact? Secret match? |
| `invalid_signature` | Same secret; clock skew; raw body not mutated |
| Tool missing after Sync | Re-sync; workspace selected; tool registered in process |
| `ctx.storage` errors | Expected without install scope — use your own DB |

More: [troubleshooting.md](./troubleshooting.md).

---

# Migrating to Native Metadata Marketplace Apps

Source: https://docs.qefro.com/docs/developer/migration-external-to-managed/

> How to migrate external backends or bespoke integrations to native Qefro Metadata Marketplace Apps (hosting: runtime).

When building business applications on Qefro (such as reservations, clinic management, appointments, or CRM extensions), migrating from bespoke external backends to **native Metadata Marketplace Apps** simplifies operations and eliminates hosting overhead.

---

## 1. The Migration Paradigm

```text
BEFORE (External Custom Backend):
  Customer Infrastructure ──▶ Custom Server ──▶ Backend SDK (POST /qefro) ──▶ Qefro SDKAdapter
  • Requires managing Docker containers, cloud hosting, and database backups.

AFTER (Native Metadata Marketplace App):
  Declarative Metadata (YAML) ──▶ Qefro Runtime
  • Zero hosting required. Qefro Runtime executes entities, workflows, storage, and UI natively.
```

---

## 2. Migration Steps

### Step 1: Map Database Tables to Entities (`entities/*.yaml`)

Instead of writing database migrations in SQL or ORMs, define your entities declaratively:

```yaml title="entities/order.yaml"
id: order
name: Order
allocate_code:
  prefix: ORD-
  start: 10001
fields:
  - name: customer_name
    type: string
    required: true
  - name: total_amount
    type: float
    required: true
  - name: status
    type: enum
    enum_values: [pending, paid, fulfilled, cancelled]
    default: pending
```

### Step 2: Convert Backend Procedures to FlowRunner Workflows (`workflows/*.yaml`)

Convert multi-step code procedures into declarative FlowRunner steps (`ask`, `tool`, `condition`, `complete`):

- Replace database `INSERT` queries with `entity.<name>.create` tools (`execution: runtime`).
- Replace authorization checks with runtime authority and Customer Hub Person bindings (`type: person`).
- Replace custom scheduling algorithms with native `entity.<name>.availability` tools.

### Step 3: Replace Custom Admin Dashboards with Metadata UI (`ui/*.yaml`)

Rather than maintaining a separate React or Vue admin panel, declare your staff views in YAML:

- Define tables and filters in `ui/pages.yaml`.
- Define navigation menus in `ui/navigation.yaml`.
- Define metric cards and charts in `ui/widgets.yaml`.

---

## 3. When NOT to Migrate (Keep as SDK Connection)

Do **not** migrate to a Marketplace App if:
1. The business system is an established enterprise ERP (e.g. Focus ERP, SAP, Oracle, ERPNext).
2. The system of record MUST live on customer premises or in a private cloud VPC.
3. The data is managed by existing legacy software with complex external transactional boundaries.

In those cases, maintain an **[External SDK Connection](/docs/developer/external-sdk-connection)** using the Qefro Backend SDK.

---

## Related Documentation

- [Integration Decision Guide](/docs/developer/integration-models)
- [Marketplace App Development Tutorial](/docs/developer/managed-marketplace-app)
- [Runtime Execution Architecture](/docs/solutions/runtime-execution)

---

# Qefro Runtime Architecture

Source: https://docs.qefro.com/docs/developer/concepts/runtime/

> Deep dive into Qefro Runtime — conversation execution, RAG, FlowRunner, entity operations, action authority, event dispatch, and security boundaries.

The **Qefro Runtime** (`ai-customer-support`) is the core multi-tenant execution engine powering the platform. It executes conversational chat, Hybrid RAG, FlowRunner state machines, Marketplace App entity operations, and external tool invocations.

```text
                                  Qefro Runtime
                                        │
    ┌──────────────────┬────────────────┼─────────────────┬─────────────────┐
    ▼                  ▼                ▼                 ▼                 ▼
Conversation          RAG          FlowRunner      Runtime Actions       Event
 Execution         Retrieval      Orchestrator        & Storage           Bus
    │                  │                │                 │                 │
Intent Match      BM25 + Dense    Step State        Entity CRUD /       Postgres
& Fast Router     Vector Ground   Machine           HTTP Executor       Idempotent
```

---

## 1. Core Responsibilities

The Runtime engine strictly separates responsibilities across the execution stack:

```text
Qefro Runtime
├── Conversation execution       # WebSocket/HTTP chat turn loop, slot harvesting
├── RAG / knowledge execution    # Query vectorization, hybrid fusion, context chunking
├── Tool/action execution        # Validation, RBAC checks, parameter stripping, invocation
├── FlowRunner                   # Deterministic multi-step state machine
├── Event handling               # Event bus persistence, idempotency, and dispatch
├── Marketplace App runtime      # Interpretation of installed YAML metadata packages
├── Entity operations            # CRUD and availability against triple-keyed storage
├── Runtime actions              # Native entity tools and generic HTTP executor calls
├── Approval/wait/resume         # Non-blocking pause for human input, upload, or approval
├── Execution state              # Durable state tracking in PostgreSQL and Redis
├── Idempotency                  # Duplicate detection via hashes and operation tokens
├── Audit logging                # Immutable security, turn, and tool invocation logs
└── Security & authority         # Runtime authority stripping and role enforcement
```

---

## 2. Model Reasoning vs. Runtime Authority

A core architectural principle of Qefro is:

> **The model is not the authority boundary.**

The LLM is a reasoning and natural-language engine, **not** an authorization or execution authority. The platform separates intent from execution through a rigorous verification pipeline:

```text
[End User Message or Event]
            │
            ▼
   Model Reasoning / Intent
   (Proposes intent and candidate action parameters)
            │
            ▼
    Candidate Action
   (e.g., `entity.reservation.create`, `tools.cancel_order`)
            │
            ▼
┌───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│              RUNTIME AUTHORIZATION BOUNDARY               │
│                                                           │
│  1. Authority Stripping:                                  │
│     Silently strips `tenant_id`, `workspace_id`,          │
│     `installation_id`, `person_id`, `created_by`          │
│                                                           │
│  2. RBAC & Permissions:                                   │
│     Verifies Org Role (Owner/Admin/Member) and App Role   │
│     (`require_entity_permission()`)                       │
│                                                           │
│  3. Expand Trust Boundary:                                │
│     Discards user/LLM `expand` controls; only accepts      │
│     admin-authored flow constants                         │
│                                                           │
│  4. Identity Injection:                                   │
│     Injects verified `person_id` from authenticated       │
│     session identity (Customer Hub)                       │
│                                                           │
│  5. Input Validation:                                     │
│     Schema types, required constraints, positive limits   │
└───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
            │
            ▼
     Actual Execution
  (RuntimeAdapter mutates database or calls external SDK)
            │
            ▼
     Event Emission
  (Emits `reservation.created` onto PostgreSQL event bus)
```

### What the LLM Can and Cannot Do

| Capability | LLM Authority | Runtime Authority |
|---|---|---|
| Propose tool parameters (name, dates, notes) | **Yes** (candidate values) | Validated against entity schema |
| Specify `tenant_id` or `workspace_id` | **No** (unconditionally stripped) | Injected from authenticated context |
| Specify `person_id` or Customer Identity | **No** (unconditionally stripped) | Injected from verified Customer Hub session |
| Execute arbitrary backend queries | **No** | Denied (only registered capabilities allowed) |
| Join/expand related entity trees | **No** (LLM expand discarded) | Controlled by admin-authored flow constants |
| Trigger database mutations directly | **No** | Routed through `RuntimeAdapter` with RBAC |

---

## 3. Four-Tier Message Routing

Every message entering the Runtime is routed through four execution tiers, maximizing performance and determinism while minimizing model compute:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  Inbound["User Turn Arrives"] --> T1{"1. Deterministic Patterns\n(Exact regex/intent match)"}
  T1 -->|Match| Exec1["Execute Flow / Action\n(Zero LLM Cost)"]
  T1 -->|Miss| T2{"2. Fast Router\n(Semantic Embedding Match)"}
  T2 -->|Cosine >= 0.82| Exec2["Trigger Matched Flow"]
  T2 -->|Miss| T3{"3. FlowRunner\n(Active Flow In-Progress?)"}
  T3 -->|Active Execution| Exec3["Feed Message as\nTrigger::Message(step)"]
  T3 -->|No Active Flow| T4["4. Agent Reasoning Loop\n(LLM analyzes context + tools)"]
  T4 --> ToolCall["Propose Candidate Actions"]
  ToolCall --> AuthCheck["Runtime Authority Check"]
  AuthCheck --> Exec4["Execute Action"]
```

1. **Deterministic Patterns:** Exact string or slash-command matches (`/cancel`, `/help`, preset options). Fast and zero LLM cost.
2. **Fast Router:** Uses dense embedding vector similarity (`cosine >= 0.82`) to map user utterances to declared flow triggers without running a full LLM turn.
3. **FlowRunner:** If an active conversation execution exists in PostgreSQL/Redis, the message is fed into the active step as a `Trigger::Message`.
4. **Agent Reasoning Loop:** If no deterministic match or active flow applies, the LLM reasons over the grounded RAG context and available tools, returning candidate tool invocations.

---

## 4. Execution State & Durability

The Runtime engine ensures resilience across long-running interactions:

### State Persistence
- **PostgreSQL:** Durable record of all conversation turns, messages, flow executions (`flow_executions` table), entity mutations, and audit events.
- **Redis:** Fast cache for active execution sessions (`active_flow_execution:{conversation_id}`) with automatic 30-day TTL and session token tracking.

### Idempotency
- Every mutation request and event carries an idempotency key (`idempotency_key` or message UUID).
- Duplicate requests return the cached result rather than re-executing steps or double-charging transactions.

### Concurrency Protection
- **Single Active Flow:** Enforced by partial unique index in PostgreSQL (`WHERE status = 'running'`). A conversation cannot run conflicting flows concurrently.
- **Optimistic Locking:** Entities support `concurrency: optimistic`, using version integers (`version: N`) to prevent lost updates during simultaneous writes.

---

## 5. Runtime Adapters: Dispatching Tool Execution

When an action is approved for execution, the Runtime dispatches it via `ExecutionBackend`:

```rust
pub enum ExecutionBackend {
    Sdk,                          // External ERP / POS / CRM tools via signed webhook
    Runtime { solution: String }, // Metadata Marketplace Apps executed by Qefro
}
```

- **Runtime (Metadata Apps):** Handled by `RuntimeAdapter`. Translates `entity.{name}.{create|list|get|update|delete|availability}` operations directly to the storage service against triple-scoped collections `(tenant_id, workspace_id, installation_id)`.
- **SDK (External Systems):** Handled by `SDKAdapter`. Dispatches an HMAC-signed HTTPS POST request (`POST /qefro`) to the external server running `@qefro-ai/backend` or `qefro-backend-sdk`.
- **Security Isolation:** Security gates (`deny_sdk_runtime_entity`, `deny_sdk_http_runtime`) strictly prevent external SDK backends from accessing or mutating native Marketplace storage entities.

---

## Related Documentation

---

# Events

Source: https://docs.qefro.com/docs/developer/concepts/events/

> Namespaced orchestration events trigger Business Flows in FlowRunner — connectors only emit.

**Orchestration events** are namespaced envelopes (`shopify.order.created`) on the org event bus. They are **triggers** into existing Business Flows — not a second workflow engine.

## Rules of thumb

1. Connectors / backends **emit only** — never start FlowRunner.
2. Event names must contain a **namespace** (dot-separated).
3. Flows opt in with `metadata.trigger: { type: 'event', event: '...' }`.
4. Production: versioning, correlation/causation, optional sequence ordering, TTL, depth/loop protection, replay APIs.

## Full guide

→ [Event-Driven Triggers](/docs/guides/event-driven-triggers)  
→ [Events API surface](/docs/developer/events/overview)  
→ [Event reference](/docs/reference/event-reference)

## Related topics

---

# FlowRunner Architecture

Source: https://docs.qefro.com/docs/developer/concepts/flows/

> FlowRunner is Qefro's deterministic business workflow state machine — triggers, lifecycle, step types, variables, idempotency, and concurrency.

**FlowRunner** (`ai-customer-support/crates/api/src/flow_engine/executor.rs`) is Qefro's deterministic business workflow execution engine. It coordinates multi-step operational logic across conversations, events, schedules, and webhooks.

There is **one canonical orchestration model** across the entire platform. Connectors, channels, and apps never maintain separate workflow engines; they all submit executions to FlowRunner.

---

## 1. Flow Triggers

Flows can be initiated through five distinct trigger sources:

```text
┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                          FLOWRUNNER TRIGGERS                           │
├──────────────────────────┬─────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ Trigger Source           │ Mechanism                                   │
├──────────────────────────┼─────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ 1. Conversational Intent │ Fast Router or Semantic Catalog matching    │
│                          │ user utterance (cosine similarity >= 0.82)  │
│ 2. Business Event        │ Event bus matches `metadata.trigger` on an  │
│                          │ emitted event (e.g., `order.created`)       │
│ 3. Schedule              │ Cron scheduler emits an event at configured │
│                          │ intervals (e.g. `0 9 * * 1`)                │
│ 4. Inbound Webhook       │ Verified webhook payload mapped directly to │
│                          │ a workflow initiation envelope              │
│ 5. Resume (Wait/Wake)    │ User response, webhook callback, human      │
│                          │ approval, or verified identity challenge    │
└──────────────────────────┴─────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

---

## 2. Flow Lifecycle

Every Flow execution progresses through a strictly monitored state machine:

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
  [*] --> Created: Trigger Fired
  Created --> Queued: Persisted in DB
  Queued --> Running: Picked by Executor
  Running --> Waiting: WaitInput / WaitApproval / WaitChallenge / Pause
  Waiting --> Resumed: User Message / Approval / Challenge Token
  Resumed --> Running: Advance Step Loop
  Running --> Completed: StepOutcome::Complete
  Running --> Failed: Max Retries / Unrecoverable Error
  Completed --> [*]
  Failed --> [*]
```

### State Definitions

- **Created:** Flow execution record instantiated with initial payload, context variables, and correlation ID.
- **Queued:** Persisted in PostgreSQL (`flow_executions` table).
- **Running:** Active in the FlowRunner step loop. Bounded by `MAX_STEPS_PER_TURN = 50` to prevent infinite loops.
- **Waiting:** Non-blocking pause. The worker releases the execution thread while awaiting:
  - `WaitInput`: User response to an `ask` step.
  - `WaitUpload`: Inbound media or file upload.
  - `WaitApproval`: Human-in-the-loop review by a supervisor in the Admin Console.
  - `WaitChallenge`: Identity verification (e.g., OTP code or SSO challenge).
  - `Pause(DateTime)`: Time delay until scheduled resume.
- **Resumed:** Reactivated via `Trigger::Message`, `Trigger::Approval`, or `Trigger::ChallengeOutput`.
- **Completed:** Terminal state. Outputs captured in `WorkingContext` for post-flow conversation follow-up.
- **Failed:** Terminal failure recorded with error code, stack context, and audit log.

---

## 3. Step Execution Primitives

FlowRunner executes declarative steps defined in metadata (`workflows/*.yaml`):

| Step Type | Description | Runtime Behavior |
|---|---|---|
| `ask` | Collect parameter from user | Prompts user, waits for reply, extracts slots, validates types, and sets variable. |
| `tool` | Execute operational action | Calls `RuntimeAdapter` (for `entity.*` CRUD) or `SDKAdapter` (for external HTTP). |
| `message` | Send informational response | Delivers message with template variable interpolation (`{{var}}`). |
| `complete` | Terminal success | Concludes the flow, summarizes results, and commits durable state. |
| `condition` | Dynamic branching | Evaluates comparison expressions (`==`, `!=`, `>`, `<`, `>=`, `<=`, `exists`). |
| `branch` | Multi-way path selector | Jumps to target step ID based on variable evaluation. |
| `upload` | File/media ingestion | Pauses execution awaiting user document or image upload. |
| `approval` | Human-in-the-loop gate | Pauses flow until an admin approves or rejects the action in the Console. |
| `challenge` | Identity challenge | Prompts for high-risk auth (e.g., OTP or phone verification) before proceeding. |
| `delay` | Scheduled sleep | Pauses execution until a specified timestamp or duration elapses. |
| `tag` | CRM categorization | Adds or removes tags on the associated Customer Hub Person. |
| `assign` | Variable assignment | Sets or transforms flow variables from expressions or previous outputs. |
| `activity` | Audit logging | Emits a business activity record into the Customer Hub timeline. |
| `notify` | Staff notification | Sends internal alert (WhatsApp, email, or Console notification) to staff. |
| `handoff` | Human agent transfer | Pauses AI interaction and routes conversation to a live agent queue. |

---

## 4. Context, Variables & Parameter Resolution

FlowRunner maintains isolated variable scopes during execution:

### Variable Sources & `input_map`
Values passed into `tool` steps use explicit dotted paths or literal prefixes:

```yaml
steps:
  - id: create_reservation
    type: tool
    tool: entity.reservation.create
    execution: runtime
    input_map:
      guest_name: customer_name          # Resolves from flow variable
      covers: party_size                 # Resolves from flow variable
      date: booking_date                 # Resolves from flow variable
      status: "$literal:confirmed"       # JSON typed literal
      source: "$literal:whatsapp"        # Literal string
```

### Dynamic Choices (`choices_from`)
When prompting users in an `ask` step, options can be dynamically queried from runtime storage:

```yaml
steps:
  - id: select_table
    type: ask
    prompt: "Which table would you prefer?"
    choices_from:
      entity: table
      filter:
        status: available
      label_field: name
      value_field: id
```

---

## 5. Idempotency, Concurrency & Audit

### One-Active-Flow Rule
FlowRunner enforces that a single conversation session can only have **one running flow execution** at any given moment. This is backed by a PostgreSQL partial unique index:

```sql
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX idx_flow_executions_one_active
ON flow_executions (conversation_id)
WHERE status = 'running';
```

If a user sends a message while a flow is running, the message is routed to the active flow step as an input or clarification, rather than spawning a competing flow.

### Retries & Error Handling
- Step-level retries are configurable (`retry: { max_attempts: 3, backoff_ms: 1000 }`).
- Failures record detailed error envelopes without exposing internal database errors to end users.
- Every state transition produces an immutable audit record in `flow_execution_steps`.

# Connectors

Source: https://docs.qefro.com/docs/developer/concepts/connectors/

> Connectors normalize external systems into Qefro events and optional tools — they never run FlowRunner.

A **connector** adapts an external product (Shopify, Odoo, HubSpot, …) into Qefro:

1. Authenticate to the external API
2. Map webhooks / polls → **namespaced events**
3. Optionally expose tools via Backend SDK or REST integrations
4. **`emit()` only** into the Qefro event bus

Connectors must not start flows, call FlowRunner, or embed a second orchestrator. Use connector-kit EventEmitter or POST /api/v1/org/events/ingest/:tenant_id.

## Build path

- Concepts: this page + [Events](/docs/developer/concepts/events)
- Per-product guides: [Integrations](/docs/integrations/overview)
- Kit reference: [Connector reference](/docs/reference/connector-reference)

## Related topics

---

# Middleware

Source: https://docs.qefro.com/docs/developer/concepts/middleware/

> Backend SDK middleware hooks around tool invocation and protocol handling.

Use SDK middleware (`app.use`) for cross-cutting concerns in **your** backend:

- Logging and metrics around `tool.invoke`
- Tenant / auth context enrichment
- Input validation and redaction

Middleware runs in your process on the signed webhook path — not inside FlowRunner step graphs.

See [Backend SDK](/docs/business-tools/backend-sdk) lifecycle.

# Approvals (developer)

Source: https://docs.qefro.com/docs/developer/concepts/approvals/

> Declare approval steps in Business Flows; operators approve in Flow Runs.

```ts
.approval({
  id: 'await_supervisor',
  prompt: 'Refund for {{order_id}} needs supervisor approval.',
})
```

- Only **Owner/Admin** can approve (API-enforced).
- Run status: `waiting_for_approval`.
- After approve, FlowRunner continues; messages deliver to the customer channel.

Operator UI: [User — Approvals](/docs/user/approvals/overview).  
Semantics: [Run Business Flows](/docs/guides/run-business-flows).

# Challenges

Source: https://docs.qefro.com/docs/developer/concepts/challenges/

> Customer verification (OTP, etc.) via Customer Provider authorize/verify and challenge/resume.

Qefro orchestrates challenges; **your** Customer Provider remains the authority.

- Implicit: tool with `auth: 'required'`
- Explicit: flow `challenge` step
- Protocol: challenge → customer response → `tool.resume`

Guides:

- [Challenge & Resume](/docs/business-tools/challenge-resume)
- [Authentication](/docs/business-tools/authentication)
- [Identity resolution](/docs/business-tools/identity-resolution)

# Memory & variables

Source: https://docs.qefro.com/docs/developer/concepts/memory/

> Conversation context, flow variables, and what the Runtime persists per run.

| Scope | What is stored |
| --- | --- |
| Conversation messages | Chat history for the channel thread |
| Flow run variables | `ask` fields, tool outputs, event payload seeds |
| Templates | `{{path}}` in prompts and complete messages |
| Event seed | `event.*` plus top-level payload keys on event-triggered runs |

There is no separate long-term “vector memory” product beyond workspace **knowledge** (RAG) and run variables.

See [Run Business Flows — Variables](/docs/guides/run-business-flows).

## Related topics

---

# Sessions

Source: https://docs.qefro.com/docs/developer/concepts/sessions/

> Channel sessions, conversation lifecycle, and how identity attaches for tools and Customer Provider.

In Qefro, a **session** is the channel-scoped context that ties messages, identity, and (optionally) verified customer state to a **conversation** inside an AI Workspace.

## Layers

| Layer | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| **Channel session** | Widget token / WhatsApp thread / API client context |
| **Conversation** | Durable message thread in a workspace |
| **Verified identity** | Result of Customer Provider / challenge — used for high-risk tools |
| **Flow run** | Separate execution record when a Business Flow is active |

Chat can exist without a flow run. A flow run may wait (`waiting_for_approval`, challenge) while the conversation stays open.

## Website widget

1. Page loads widget with workspace/public configuration.
2. Widget obtains a **session token** for the channel.
3. Optional `identify()` attaches a known customer subject (see identity docs).
4. Messages create or continue a **conversation**.
5. Tool calls may require Customer Provider authorization against session attributes.

## WhatsApp

- Thread identity is typically the **phone number** (provider-verified).
- Conversation mapping is workspace + channel + external thread key.
- Same Runtime and tools as widget; channel packaging differs.

## API / Employee channels

- Org JWT or internal portal session for **employees**.
- Customer chat APIs use channel credentials, not employee RBAC.

## Relationship to memory

Session and conversation IDs scope what [Memory](/docs/developer/concepts/memory) and flow variables can see. Do not put secrets in client-visible session metadata.

## Related topics

---

# JavaScript / TypeScript SDK

Source: https://docs.qefro.com/docs/developer/sdk/javascript/

> Use @qefro-ai/backend to register tools, flows, customer provider, and signed webhooks.

The **Qefro SDK** (`@qefro-ai/backend`) runs in **your** backend to
connect an external ERP / POS / CRM over signed `POST /qefro`. It is
**not** how you build a Marketplace App — those are metadata packages
executed by Qefro Runtime
([Runtime vs SDK](/docs/solutions/runtime-vs-sdk)).

```bash
npm install @qefro-ai/backend
export QEFRO_SIGNING_SECRET="your-signing-secret"
```

```ts
const app = new Qefro({ signingSecret: process.env.QEFRO_SIGNING_SECRET! });

app.tool(
  {
    name: 'order_status_check',
    description: 'Look up order by ID',
    auth: 'none',
    input_schema: {
      type: 'object',
      properties: { order_id: { type: 'string' } },
      required: ['order_id'],
    },
  },
  async (ctx) => {
    return { found: true, status: 'shipped', order_id: ctx.parameters.order_id };
  },
);

await app.listen({ port: 8088, path: '/qefro' });
```

## Learn more

- [Backend SDK Integration](/docs/business-tools/backend-sdk)
- [Register SDK Business Tools](/docs/guides/register-sdk-business-tools)
- [Define Business Flows](/docs/guides/define-business-flows)
- [Event-Driven Triggers](/docs/guides/event-driven-triggers)
- Example: [event-abandoned-cart](https://github.com/qefro-ai/qefro-js-backend-sdk/tree/main/examples/event-abandoned-cart)

## Related topics

# Python SDK

Source: https://docs.qefro.com/docs/developer/sdk/python/

> Use qefro-backend to register tools and flows over the signed Qefro webhook protocol.

The **Qefro Python SDK** (`qefro-backend`) connects **external** systems
to Qefro over `/qefro`. Marketplace Apps do not use this package — see
[Runtime vs SDK](/docs/solutions/runtime-vs-sdk).

```bash
pip install qefro-backend
export QEFRO_SIGNING_SECRET="your-signing-secret"
```

```python
from qefro_backend import Qefro

app = Qefro(signing_secret="...")  # or env

@app.tool({
    "name": "order_status_check",
    "description": "Look up order by ID",
    "auth": "none",
    "input_schema": {
        "type": "object",
        "properties": {"order_id": {"type": "string"}},
        "required": ["order_id"],
    },
})
def order_status(ctx):
    return {"found": True, "status": "shipped", "order_id": ctx.parameters["order_id"]}

app.run(8088)  # POST /qefro
```

- [Event-Driven Triggers](/docs/guides/event-driven-triggers)

# Rust SDK

Source: https://docs.qefro.com/docs/developer/sdk/rust/

> Use qefro-backend-sdk to register tools and flows with typed metadata.

The **Qefro Rust SDK** (`qefro-backend-sdk`) connects **external** systems
to Qefro over `/qefro`. Marketplace Apps do not use this crate — see
[Runtime vs SDK](/docs/solutions/runtime-vs-sdk).

```bash
cargo add qefro-backend-sdk
```

```rust
use qefro_backend_sdk::BusinessFlowMetadata;

// app.tool(...) then:
app.flow(BusinessFlowMetadata {
    id: "order_lookup".into(),
    name: Some("Order Lookup".into()),
    intent: vec!["track order".into()],
    ..Default::default()
})?
.ask("email", "email", "Please enter your email.")
.tool("lookup", "lookup_customer")
.complete("done", None)?;
```

# Working with events

Source: https://docs.qefro.com/docs/developer/events/overview/

> Emit, list, retry, and replay orchestration events; match flows with trigger.event.

## Emit

## Operate

| Method | Path | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| GET | `/api/v1/org/events` | List |
| GET | `/api/v1/org/events/:id` | Get |
| POST | `/api/v1/org/events/:id/retry` | Retry failed |
| POST | `/api/v1/org/events/:id/replay` | Replay as new row |
| POST | `/api/v1/org/events/replay` | Range replay |

# Webhooks

Source: https://docs.qefro.com/docs/developer/webhooks/overview/

> Inbound provider webhooks Qefro consumes and webhook-style flow triggers.

Two different “webhook” ideas:

1. **Provider webhooks Qefro consumes** — Razorpay billing, Meta WhatsApp — see [API Webhooks](/docs/api/webhooks).
2. **Your Backend SDK webhook** — Qefro calls `POST /qefro` on your server — see [External SDK Connection](/docs/developer/external-sdk-connection).
3. **Flow trigger `type: webhook`** — named ingest into the event bus — see [Event-Driven Triggers](/docs/guides/event-driven-triggers).

# Schedules

Source: https://docs.qefro.com/docs/developer/schedules/overview/

> Cron triggers on Business Flows — the ticker emits schedule events into the bus.

```ts
app.flow({
  id: 'nightly_reconciliation',
  trigger: { type: 'schedule', cron: '0 2 * * *' },
})
  .tool({ id: 'run', tool_ref: 'reconcile_orders' })
  .complete({ id: 'done' });
```

On Sync Tools, the Runtime upserts a tenant schedule. The ticker emits `schedule.<flow_id>`; dispatch starts FlowRunner.

Details: [Event-Driven Triggers — Schedule](/docs/guides/event-driven-triggers).

# Shopify integration

Source: https://docs.qefro.com/docs/integrations/shopify/overview/

> Connect Shopify to Qefro — Marketplace app, OAuth, events, tools. Shopify does not use the SDK.

# Shopify

Ideal for abandoned cart recovery and order tracking solutions.

Shopify on Qefro is a **metadata Marketplace App** executed by generic Runtime
HTTP. There is no Shopify SDK, connector process, or <code>/qefro</code> webhook
in the app package. SDK connections remain for Focus ERP / Yaaz.

## Installation

1. Install the **Shopify** Marketplace app on the target AI Workspace.
2. In the workspace **Tools** tab, **Connect Shopify**: shop domain plus **that tenant’s** Shopify app client ID and secret.
3. Chat tools use the workspace HTTP connection (shop host + encrypted Admin API token).
4. Webhooks POST to Qefro `/webhooks/http/shopify`. HMAC is verified with **that workspace’s** app secret on the raw body; topics map to Business Events via package metadata, then `orchestration_events` → CRM Automation.

Operator steps: [Connect Shopify](/docs/user/how-to/connect-shopify).
Package internals: [shopify-runtime](/docs/solutions/examples/shopify-runtime).

## Authentication

OAuth authorization code. Client id/secret are entered per workspace at
Connect and encrypted at rest. Shop domain is validated (`*.myshopify.com`);
OAuth `state` is workspace- and session-bound. Workspace A cannot steal
workspace B’s shop.

Do not put Shopify app secrets in package YAML or process environment.

## Events

| Event name | Source topic (metadata) |
| --- | --- |
| `order.created` | `orders/create` |
| `order.updated` | `orders/updated` |
| `order.cancelled` | `orders/cancelled` |
| `customer.created` | `customers/create` |
| `customer.updated` | `customers/update` |

Envelope fields (idempotency, correlation, TTL): [Event reference](/docs/reference/event-reference).

## Tools

Lookup products, customers, and orders through generic HTTP tools
(`read_products`, `read_customers`, `read_orders`). **Staff** Console can
list the shop. **Customers** on WhatsApp/widget see only their own orders
(Hub email, OTP if needed, ownership after the response). Missing scopes
reject execution. Keep PII minimization and least privilege.

Details: [HTTP tools](/docs/solutions/http-tools).

## Webhooks

1. Receive provider webhook at the generic Qefro endpoint.
2. Identify the workspace from the shop identity header (selects that tenant’s app secret).
3. Verify HMAC on the raw body with that secret (constant-time). Reject missing/invalid signatures.
4. Map topic → Business Event via metadata; emit onto `orchestration_events`.
5. CRM Automation consumes the bus. Replay uses the Shopify webhook id.

## Workflow checklist

## Related topics

---

# WooCommerce integration

Source: https://docs.qefro.com/docs/integrations/woocommerce/overview/

> Connect WooCommerce to Qefro — installation, auth, events, tools, and examples.

# WooCommerce

WordPress-hosted stores; map webhooks to namespaced events.

Namespace convention: events under <code>woocommerce.*</code>. Connectors emit only; FlowRunner stays in Qefro.

## Installation

1. Deploy or enable the WooCommerce connector service (Qefro connectors monorepo / your fork).
2. Configure credentials (below) and `QEFRO_API_BASE_URL`, `QEFRO_TENANT_ID`, API token.
3. Point external webhooks at the connector public URL (not directly at FlowRunner).
4. In Qefro, declare flows with `trigger.event` matching emitted names — [Event-Driven Triggers](/docs/guides/event-driven-triggers).
5. Sync SDK tools if the connector exposes Backend SDK handlers.

## Authentication

WooCommerce REST API keys (consumer key/secret).

Store secrets in the connector environment or secret manager — not in flow metadata.

## Events

| Event name | Notes |
| --- | --- |
| `woocommerce.order.created` | Emit when source system notifies connector |
| `woocommerce.order.updated` | Emit when source system notifies connector |
| `woocommerce.cart.abandoned` | Emit when source system notifies connector |

Envelope fields (idempotency, correlation, TTL): [Event reference](/docs/reference/event-reference).

## Tools

Typical tool surface: **order status, refund request**.

Implement as Backend SDK tools or REST Business Tools. Keep PII minimization and least privilege scopes.

## Webhooks

1. Receive provider webhook → verify signature.
2. Normalize payload → `EventEmitter.emit({ name: 'woocommerce.…', payload, idempotencyKey })`.
3. Return 2xx quickly; let Qefro dispatch asynchronously.

## Examples

- Abandoned cart pattern: [Solutions — Abandoned cart](/docs/solutions/abandoned-cart) (Shopify-oriented; adapt event names).
- Order tracking: [Solutions — Order tracking](/docs/solutions/order-tracking).

## Workflow checklist

## Related topics

# Stripe integration

Source: https://docs.qefro.com/docs/integrations/stripe/overview/

> Connect Stripe to Qefro — installation, auth, events, tools, and examples.

# Stripe

Prefer verifying Stripe signatures in the connector, then emit to Qefro.

Namespace convention: events under <code>stripe.*</code>. Connectors emit only; FlowRunner stays in Qefro.

## Installation

1. Deploy or enable the Stripe connector service (Qefro connectors monorepo / your fork).
2. Configure credentials (below) and `QEFRO_API_BASE_URL`, `QEFRO_TENANT_ID`, API token.
3. Point external webhooks at the connector public URL (not directly at FlowRunner).
4. In Qefro, declare flows with `trigger.event` matching emitted names — [Event-Driven Triggers](/docs/guides/event-driven-triggers).
5. Sync SDK tools if the connector exposes Backend SDK handlers.

## Authentication

Restricted API keys; verify Stripe webhook signatures before emit.

Store secrets in the connector environment or secret manager — not in flow metadata.

## Events

| Event name | Notes |
| --- | --- |
| `stripe.invoice.paid` | Emit when source system notifies connector |
| `stripe.invoice.payment_failed` | Emit when source system notifies connector |
| `stripe.customer.subscription.updated` | Emit when source system notifies connector |

Envelope fields (idempotency, correlation, TTL): [Event reference](/docs/reference/event-reference).

## Tools

Typical tool surface: **invoice lookup, subscription status**.

Implement as Backend SDK tools or REST Business Tools. Keep PII minimization and least privilege scopes.

## Webhooks

1. Receive provider webhook → verify signature.
2. Normalize payload → `EventEmitter.emit({ name: 'stripe.…', payload, idempotencyKey })`.
3. Return 2xx quickly; let Qefro dispatch asynchronously.

## Examples

- Abandoned cart pattern: [Solutions — Abandoned cart](/docs/solutions/abandoned-cart) (Shopify-oriented; adapt event names).
- Order tracking: [Solutions — Order tracking](/docs/solutions/order-tracking).

## Workflow checklist

## Related topics

# Razorpay integration

Source: https://docs.qefro.com/docs/integrations/razorpay/overview/

> Connect Razorpay to Qefro — installation, auth, events, tools, and examples.

# Razorpay

Platform billing webhooks: see API Webhooks. Connector events are separate namespaced emits for your tenant flows.

Namespace convention: events under <code>razorpay.*</code>. Connectors emit only; FlowRunner stays in Qefro.

## Installation

1. Deploy or enable the Razorpay connector service (Qefro connectors monorepo / your fork).
2. Configure credentials (below) and `QEFRO_API_BASE_URL`, `QEFRO_TENANT_ID`, API token.
3. Point external webhooks at the connector public URL (not directly at FlowRunner).
4. In Qefro, declare flows with `trigger.event` matching emitted names — [Event-Driven Triggers](/docs/guides/event-driven-triggers).
5. Sync SDK tools if the connector exposes Backend SDK handlers.

## Authentication

Key id/secret; Qefro also consumes billing webhooks for SaaS entitlements.

Store secrets in the connector environment or secret manager — not in flow metadata.

## Events

| Event name | Notes |
| --- | --- |
| `razorpay.payment.captured` | Emit when source system notifies connector |
| `razorpay.payment.failed` | Emit when source system notifies connector |

Envelope fields (idempotency, correlation, TTL): [Event reference](/docs/reference/event-reference).

## Tools

Typical tool surface: **payment lookup**.

Implement as Backend SDK tools or REST Business Tools. Keep PII minimization and least privilege scopes.

## Webhooks

1. Receive provider webhook → verify signature.
2. Normalize payload → `EventEmitter.emit({ name: 'razorpay.…', payload, idempotencyKey })`.
3. Return 2xx quickly; let Qefro dispatch asynchronously.

## Examples

- Abandoned cart pattern: [Solutions — Abandoned cart](/docs/solutions/abandoned-cart) (Shopify-oriented; adapt event names).
- Order tracking: [Solutions — Order tracking](/docs/solutions/order-tracking).

# Zendesk

Use for human handoff bridges and ticket status tools.

Namespace convention: events under <code>zendesk.*</code>. Connectors emit only; FlowRunner stays in Qefro.

## Installation

1. Deploy or enable the Zendesk connector service (Qefro connectors monorepo / your fork).
2. Configure credentials (below) and `QEFRO_API_BASE_URL`, `QEFRO_TENANT_ID`, API token.
3. Point external webhooks at the connector public URL (not directly at FlowRunner).
4. In Qefro, declare flows with `trigger.event` matching emitted names — [Event-Driven Triggers](/docs/guides/event-driven-triggers).
5. Sync SDK tools if the connector exposes Backend SDK handlers.

## Authentication

API token + email or OAuth.

Store secrets in the connector environment or secret manager — not in flow metadata.

## Events

| Event name | Notes |
| --- | --- |
| `zendesk.ticket.created` | Emit when source system notifies connector |
| `zendesk.ticket.solved` | Emit when source system notifies connector |

Envelope fields (idempotency, correlation, TTL): [Event reference](/docs/reference/event-reference).

## Tools

Typical tool surface: **ticket get, ticket comment**.

Implement as Backend SDK tools or REST Business Tools. Keep PII minimization and least privilege scopes.

## Webhooks

1. Receive provider webhook → verify signature.
2. Normalize payload → `EventEmitter.emit({ name: 'zendesk.…', payload, idempotencyKey })`.
3. Return 2xx quickly; let Qefro dispatch asynchronously.

## Examples

- Abandoned cart pattern: [Solutions — Abandoned cart](/docs/solutions/abandoned-cart) (Shopify-oriented; adapt event names).
- Order tracking: [Solutions — Order tracking](/docs/solutions/order-tracking).

# Solutions (outcomes)

# Solution Development

Source: https://docs.qefro.com/docs/solutions/overview/

> Build installable Marketplace Apps as metadata packages executed by Qefro Runtime — entities, UI, flows, events. SDK is for external systems only.

**Solution Development** is how you build complete, branded business
applications on Qefro: a restaurant manager, a clinic front desk, a real
estate CRM, a booking product — shipped as a single **installable
package**.

A **Qefro Marketplace App** is a **declarative package**, not an SDK
server. Developers do **not** need a backend to create Restaurant, Clinic,
Real Estate, Booking, or CRM apps. Qefro Runtime executes the metadata:
UI, entities, storage, Business Flows, Business Events, CRM, and
Automation.

**Default developer story:**

```text
Developer → Create App Metadata → Validate → Package → Publish
  → Install into Workspace → Qefro Runtime
```

```bash
qefro app init restaurant-pro
qefro app validate restaurant-pro
qefro app package restaurant-pro
qefro app install restaurant-pro
```

**Start here:** [Build your first app](/docs/solutions/build-your-first-app)
using [`restaurant-pro-runtime`](/docs/solutions/examples/restaurant-pro-runtime).

:::info Runtime vs SDK
**Build a Qefro Marketplace App with metadata.** Use the SDK only to
connect an external ERP, POS, or CRM. See [Runtime vs SDK](/docs/solutions/runtime-vs-sdk).
:::

## What is a Qefro Marketplace App?

An installable YAML package with `hosting: runtime`. Identity, entities,
workflows, events, UI, and permissions live in the package. After install,
Qefro Runtime:

- renders dashboards, tables, forms, detail pages, navigation, and widgets
- persists entities in [managed storage](/docs/solutions/managed-storage) (no direct DB)
- compiles `workflows/` into the same **BusinessFlow / FlowRunner** as every other flow
- emits business events that CRM Automation can consume
- hosts Contacts (`host: contacts`) and Automations (`host: automations`)

You never run `npm run dev` on a `/qefro` process for this path.

## What you can build

Any business domain that fits entities + flows + UI:

| Domain | Typical pages | Data plane |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Restaurant | Dashboard, reservations, tables, menu | Runtime entities + managed storage |
| Clinic | Appointments, patients, schedule | Runtime entities + managed storage |
| Real estate | Properties, leads, viewings | Runtime entities + managed storage |
| Commerce | Products, customers, orders | Generic Runtime HTTP (Shopify) or entities |
| CRM / booking | Pipeline, contacts, bookings | Runtime entities + Person CRM |

Canonical references:

| Package | App id | Role |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [restaurant-pro-runtime](/docs/solutions/examples/restaurant-pro-runtime) | `restaurant-pro-runtime` | Hospitality metadata app |
| [real-estate-runtime](/docs/solutions/examples/real-estate-runtime) | `real-estate-runtime` | Same model, different nouns |
| [shopify-runtime](/docs/solutions/examples/shopify-runtime) | `shopify-runtime` | Commerce metadata + generic Runtime HTTP |

Collection repo: [qefro-marketplace-apps](https://github.com/qefro-ai/qefro-marketplace-apps)
([index](/docs/solutions/examples/marketplace-apps)).

All Marketplace applications are built natively as metadata packages (`hosting: runtime`). To integrate an existing enterprise backend or external database, use an [External SDK Connection](/docs/developer/external-sdk-connection).

## Core principles

1. **Metadata is the application.** `hosting: runtime` packages ship
   `manifest.yaml`, `entities/`, `workflows/`, and `ui/`. No SDK process.
2. **UI is declarative data.** Theme, nav, pages, and widgets are YAML —
   no package JS in the portal UI (no iframes, no injected scripts).
3. **Storage is Qefro-managed.** Entity tools such as
   `entity.reservation.create` persist documents. No Mongo connection, no
   direct `storage/*` from YAML.
4. **Flows compile to FlowRunner.** `ask` → `tool` → `condition` →
   `approval` / `challenge` → `complete` on the same engine as every
   Business Flow.
5. **Capability mediation is mandatory.** Host interactions pass through
   the capability registry.
6. **Event-driven communication is mandatory.** Business events drive
   automation; `ui.*` events are observational.

### Platform rules

These rules are enforced at publish time and at render time. Packages that
violate them are rejected:

| # | Rule |
| --- | --- |
| 1 | No arbitrary JavaScript |
| 2 | No direct DOM access |
| 3 | No iframe execution |
| 4 | No direct database access |
| 5 | No direct Redis access |
| 6 | No direct network access |
| 7 | Capability mediation is mandatory |
| 8 | Event-driven communication is mandatory |

See [Security model](/docs/solutions/security) for how each rule is enforced.

## The delivery pipeline

```mermaid
flowchart TB
    A[Marketplace App package<br/>manifest · entities · workflows · ui] --> B[Registry]
    B --> C[Installer]
    C --> D[Qefro Runtime]
    D --> FR[FlowRunner]
    D --> S[Managed storage]
    D --> G[Portal renderer]
    D --> CRM[Person CRM · Automations]
```

| Stage | Responsibility | Details |
| --- | --- | --- |
| App package | Metadata: manifest, entities, workflows, UI | [Package structure](#package-structure) |
| Registry | Signed global catalog (platform-admin publish only) | [Publishing](/docs/solutions/publishing) |
| Installer | Activation, capabilities, workspace install | [Installation](/docs/solutions/installation) |
| Qefro Runtime | UI, entity tools, FlowRunner, events | [Architecture](/docs/solutions/architecture) |
| Managed storage | Documents for declared entities | [Managed storage](/docs/solutions/managed-storage) |
| Portal renderer | Dashboards, tables, forms, widgets | [Pages](/docs/solutions/pages) |

External ERP / POS / CRM integrations take a **separate** path: SDK →
`/qefro` → Runtime. See [Runtime vs SDK](/docs/solutions/runtime-vs-sdk).

## Package structure

Prefer `qefro app init <id>`. The implemented tree
(from `restaurant-pro-runtime` / `qefro app init`) is:

```text
my-app/
├── manifest.yaml        # identity, hosting: runtime, entities, flows, events, UI, permissions
├── entities/            # domain schemas (required for hosting: runtime)
│   └── record.yaml
├── workflows/           # Business Flows → FlowRunner
│   └── create-record.yaml
└── ui/                  # Runtime-rendered staff UI
    ├── theme.yaml
    ├── navigation.yaml
    ├── pages.yaml
    ├── layouts.yaml
    ├── widgets.yaml
    └── sources.yaml     # type: entity | runtime
```

There is no `src/`, no `events/` directory, and no `automations/`
directory. Events are declared on the manifest (`events:`). Automations
are a portal host page (`host: automations`), not package files.

YAML is assembled into a canonical JSON package, checksummed and signed —
see [Packaging](/docs/solutions/packaging).

## How this differs from playbooks

[Solution playbooks](/docs/solutions/playbooks) are outcome-oriented guides
that compose *existing* platform features (customer support, order tracking,
refunds). Solution Development produces **new installable packages** with
their own manifest, entities, UI, and workflows.

## Related platform concepts

- [Runtime](/docs/developer/concepts/runtime) — the execution engine that runs installed workflows.
- [Events](/docs/developer/concepts/events) — the platform event bus that solutions ride.
- [Managed storage](/docs/solutions/managed-storage) — document plane for declared entities.
- [Connectors](/docs/developer/concepts/connectors) — stateless integration containers behind the bridge.
- [Business Flows](/docs/developer/concepts/flows) — the flow model workflows compile to.
- [External SDK Connection](/docs/developer/external-sdk-connection) — ERP / POS / CRM → SDK → `/qefro`.

# Customer support

Source: https://docs.qefro.com/docs/solutions/customer-support/

> Grounded support assistant on website and WhatsApp with optional Business Tools and human handoff.

Grounded support assistant on website and WhatsApp with optional Business Tools and human handoff.

## Architecture

Widget/WhatsApp → Customer AI → Hybrid RAG + tools → handoff webhook

## Prerequisites

- Organization + Support workspace
- Knowledge documents uploaded
- Optional SDK tools for account actions

## Installation

1. Complete [User getting started](/docs/user/getting-started) for the Support (or commerce) workspace.
2. Connect channels required by this solution.
3. Register tools / connectors (see links below).
4. Declare and **enable** flows; Accept versions after sync.
5. Run a dry-end-to-end test in a non-production workspace when possible.

## Flows

Conversation-triggered flows for cancel/refund; knowledge for FAQs.

## Deployment

- Production checklist: [Production deployment](/docs/guides/production-deployment)
- Observe Flow Runs and `/api/v1/org/events` for event-driven paths

## Troubleshooting

- No answer / weak citations → knowledge coverage ([Knowledge Base](/docs/user/knowledge-base/overview))
- Tool failures → tool logs + SDK webhook health
- Event flow never starts → namespaced name, Enabled+Valid+Accepted, `when` predicate ([Events](/docs/guides/event-driven-triggers))
- Approval stuck → Owner/Admin role ([Approvals](/docs/user/approvals/overview))

## Learn more

- [Build AI customer support](/docs/guides/build-ai-customer-support)
- [Deploy widget](/docs/guides/deploy-website-widget)
- [Deploy WhatsApp](/docs/guides/deploy-whatsapp-ai)

## Related topics

# WhatsApp commerce

Source: https://docs.qefro.com/docs/solutions/whatsapp-commerce/

> Sell and support on WhatsApp with grounded product answers, order tools, and optional event-driven journeys.

**Outcome:** Customers discover products, get policy-correct answers, check orders, and complete guided commerce tasks on **WhatsApp** — backed by the same workspace Runtime as your website.

## Building blocks

| Piece | Role |
| --- | --- |
| Customer AI workspace | Knowledge + instructions |
| WhatsApp channel | [Configure WhatsApp](/docs/user/how-to/configure-whatsapp) |
| Catalog / order tools | Shopify HTTP tools (customer-scoped orders) or custom SDK |
| Identity | Customer Hub Person; WhatsApp email OTP when orders need `{person.email}` |
| Flows | Checkout help, abandoned cart, returns |
| Events | Cart/checkout webhooks → FlowRunner |

## Operator path

1. [Create an AI agent](/docs/user/how-to/create-ai-agent) for commerce/support.
2. Connect store — [Connect Shopify](/docs/user/how-to/connect-shopify) or WooCommerce integration.
3. [Configure WhatsApp](/docs/user/how-to/configure-whatsapp) on that workspace.
4. Test order tracking and FAQs on a real device. WhatsApp “show my recent orders” should ask for email + OTP if Hub has no email, then return **only that customer’s** orders.
5. Add journeys: [Abandoned cart](/docs/solutions/abandoned-cart), [Order tracking](/docs/solutions/order-tracking), [Refund automation](/docs/solutions/refund-automation).

## Workflow

## Related topics

# Order tracking

Source: https://docs.qefro.com/docs/solutions/order-tracking/

> Customers ask where their order is; the assistant calls your order API via a Business Tool or flow.

Customers ask where their order is; the assistant calls your order API via a Business Tool or flow.

## Architecture

For **Shopify** Marketplace: customer chat → `list_my_orders` / `get_my_order` → generic HTTP executor → Admin API filtered by Hub `{person.email}` → ownership check.

For **SDK / custom API**: chat intent → flow or tool_loop → order_status_check → cited/status response.

See [HTTP tools](/docs/solutions/http-tools) and [Connect Shopify](/docs/user/how-to/connect-shopify).

## Prerequisites

- Order status API or Backend SDK tool
- Workspace with tool enabled
- Clear intent utterances

## Installation

1. Complete [User getting started](/docs/user/getting-started) for the Support (or commerce) workspace.
2. Connect channels required by this solution.
3. Register tools / connectors (see links below).
4. Declare and **enable** flows; Accept versions after sync.
5. Run a dry-end-to-end test in a non-production workspace when possible.

## Flows

ask order_id → tool order_status_check → complete with `{{status}}`

## Deployment

- Production checklist: [Production deployment](/docs/guides/production-deployment)
- Observe Flow Runs and `/api/v1/org/events` for event-driven paths

## Troubleshooting

- No answer / weak citations → knowledge coverage ([Knowledge Base](/docs/user/knowledge-base/overview))
- Tool failures → tool logs + SDK webhook health
- Event flow never starts → namespaced name, Enabled+Valid+Accepted, `when` predicate ([Events](/docs/guides/event-driven-triggers))
- Approval stuck → Owner/Admin role ([Approvals](/docs/user/approvals/overview))

## Learn more

- [Define flows](/docs/guides/define-business-flows)
- [Register SDK tools](/docs/guides/register-sdk-business-tools)
- [Order approval example pattern](/docs/guides/run-business-flows)

## Related topics

# Lead qualification

Source: https://docs.qefro.com/docs/solutions/lead-qualification/

> Capture and qualify leads via chat or WhatsApp, then hand off to CRM or sales.

**Outcome:** Website or WhatsApp visitors are guided through qualifying questions; good-fit leads are captured and pushed to your CRM or notify sales.

## Architecture (business view)

1. **Customer AI workspace** with product/pricing knowledge.
2. **Flow or structured prompts** collect company size, use case, timeline.
3. **Business Tool** creates/updates HubSpot (or other CRM) lead/contact.
4. Optional **approval or human handoff** for enterprise tier.
5. Optional **event** from marketing site form → same flow via [event-driven triggers](/docs/guides/event-driven-triggers).

## Prerequisites

- Workspace + knowledge for accurate product answers
- CRM tool (HubSpot integration or custom SDK tool) — [HubSpot](/docs/integrations/hubspot/overview)
- Clear definition of qualified vs disqualified
- Channel: widget and/or WhatsApp

## Operator checklist

## Troubleshooting

| Issue | Direction |
| --- | --- |
| Leads missing in CRM | Tool logs; field mapping; auth |
| Low quality leads | Tighten questions; add disqualify paths |
| Spam | Rate limits, challenge, or human review step |

## Related topics

# Conversational commerce

Source: https://docs.qefro.com/docs/solutions/conversational-commerce/

> Assist shoppers on WhatsApp/web with catalog answers, order actions, and event-driven lifecycle messages.

Assist shoppers on WhatsApp/web with catalog answers, order actions, and event-driven lifecycle messages.

## Architecture

Channels + RAG catalog + tools + event triggers for post-purchase

## Prerequisites

- Commerce connector
- Customer AI channel
- Tools for catalog/order
- Event flows for shipping updates

## Installation

1. Complete [User getting started](/docs/user/getting-started) for the Support (or commerce) workspace.
2. Connect channels required by this solution.
3. Register tools / connectors (see links below).
4. Declare and **enable** flows; Accept versions after sync.
5. Run a dry-end-to-end test in a non-production workspace when possible.

## Flows

Mix conversation flows (browse/buy help) and event flows (shipped, delivered)

## Deployment

- Production checklist: [Production deployment](/docs/guides/production-deployment)
- Observe Flow Runs and `/api/v1/org/events` for event-driven paths

## Troubleshooting

- No answer / weak citations → knowledge coverage ([Knowledge Base](/docs/user/knowledge-base/overview))
- Tool failures → tool logs + SDK webhook health
- Event flow never starts → namespaced name, Enabled+Valid+Accepted, `when` predicate ([Events](/docs/guides/event-driven-triggers))
- Approval stuck → Owner/Admin role ([Approvals](/docs/user/approvals/overview))

## Learn more

- [WhatsApp](/docs/user/channels/whatsapp)
- [Integrations](/docs/integrations/overview)
- [Event-Driven Triggers](/docs/guides/event-driven-triggers)

# CLI

Source: https://docs.qefro.com/docs/reference/cli/

> qefro CLI for Marketplace Apps and platform operations.

The **`qefro`** CLI lives in `qefro-plugin-platform/services/qefro-cli`.
Primary product configuration is still the **Admin Console**.

## Marketplace Apps (default)

```text
qefro app init <id> [--name NAME]
qefro app validate [dir]
qefro app package [dir]
qefro app install <name> [--version V] [--settings JSON]
```

`app init` aliases `create-app` and always scaffolds a **metadata
Marketplace App** (`hosting: runtime`). See
[Build your first app](/docs/solutions/build-your-first-app).

## Also available

```text
qefro create-app <id> [--name NAME] [--hosting runtime|external]
                                                    [--endpoint URL] [--minimal]
qefro dev [dir]
qefro publish [dir]
qefro register --endpoint URL [--solution ID]
qefro solution build|publish|install|list
qefro workflow trigger|list|logs
qefro replay <execution-id>
```

`--hosting external` scaffolds an SDK `/qefro` process for connecting an
**external** ERP, POS, or CRM. `hosting: managed` is not supported.
See [Runtime vs SDK](/docs/solutions/runtime-vs-sdk).

Environment: `QEFRO_SOLUTION_URL`, `QEFRO_RUNTIME_URL`, `QEFRO_TENANT_ID`,
`QEFRO_ORGANIZATION_ID`, `QEFRO_PUBLISHER_ID`, `QEFRO_SIGNING_KEY_HEX` /
`QEFRO_KEYS_FILE`, `QEFRO_INTERNAL_BEARER`.

Language SDKs (`@qefro-ai/backend`, `qefro-backend`, `qefro-backend-sdk`)
are libraries embedded in **your** ERP/POS/CRM connector — they are not
required to build a Marketplace App.

## Related topics

---

# Environment variables

Source: https://docs.qefro.com/docs/reference/environment-variables/

> Common environment variables for Backend SDK, connectors, and self-hosted components.

Never commit secrets. Prefer a secret manager in production.

## Backend SDK

| Variable | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `QEFRO_SIGNING_SECRET` | Shared secret for webhook signature verify/sign |
| `PORT` | HTTP port for `/qefro` (examples) |

## Event emit / connectors

| Variable | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `QEFRO_API_BASE_URL` | e.g. `https://api.qefro.com` |
| `QEFRO_TENANT_ID` | Tenant UUID for ingest path |
| `QEFRO_API_TOKEN` | Bearer token for emit APIs |

## Self-hosted control plane

See deployment/docker/kubernetes docs for Postgres, Redis, JWT, object storage, and model endpoints. Variable names are environment-specific.

# Configuration

Source: https://docs.qefro.com/docs/reference/configuration/

> Where Qefro settings live — Admin Console, SDK metadata, and connector config.

| Layer | What you configure |
| --- | --- |
| Admin Console | Workspaces, knowledge, channels, RBAC, SDK connections, enable flows |
| Backend SDK | Tools, flows, customer provider, middleware (code) |
| Connectors | External credentials, webhook secrets, emit target |
| Platform env | Self-host infrastructure only |

Flow **Prompt Overrides** and enable toggles are console-side and survive SDK `name` renames (identity is flow `id`).

# Event reference

Source: https://docs.qefro.com/docs/reference/event-reference/

> Orchestration event envelope fields, statuses, naming rules, and HTTP APIs.

Canonical guide with examples: [Event-Driven Triggers](/docs/guides/event-driven-triggers).

## Naming

- Required form: `namespace.entity.action` (must contain `.`)
- Segments: `a-zA-Z0-9_-`, non-empty, max name length 256
- Examples: `shopify.cart.abandoned`, `schedule.nightly_reconciliation`, `system.flow.completed`

## Envelope fields

| Field | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | yes | Namespaced event name |
| `source` | no | Producer label |
| `payload` | no | JSON object |
| `version` | no | Default `1.0` |
| `correlation_id` | no | Business process correlation |
| `causation_id` | no | Parent event id |
| `idempotency_key` | no | Tenant-unique dedupe |
| `sequence_key` + `sequence_n` | no | FIFO stream (both required) |
| `expires_at` / `ttl_seconds` | no | Expiration |
| `depth` | no | Loop protection hop count (default max 8) |
| `delay_seconds` | no | Delay before claim |

## Statuses

`received`, `validated`, `queued`, `running`, `completed`, `failed`, `retry`, `dead_letter`, `expired`

## HTTP APIs

| Method | Path |
| --- | --- |
| GET | `/api/v1/org/events` |
| POST | `/api/v1/org/events` |
| GET | `/api/v1/org/events/:id` |
| POST | `/api/v1/org/events/:id/retry` |
| POST | `/api/v1/org/events/:id/replay` |
| POST | `/api/v1/org/events/replay` |
| POST | `/api/v1/org/events/ingest/:tenant_id` |

Also listed under [REST APIs](/docs/api/rest-apis).

## Related topics

# Connector reference

Source: https://docs.qefro.com/docs/reference/connector-reference/

> Contracts for Qefro connectors — EventEmitter, naming, and boundaries.

## Boundary

Connectors MUST only emit events (and optionally host tools via Backend SDK). They MUST NOT start flows or call FlowRunner.

## EventEmitter (connector-kit)

Typical options:

- `baseUrl` — `QEFRO_API_BASE_URL`
- `tenantId` — `QEFRO_TENANT_ID`
- `token` — `QEFRO_API_TOKEN`
- `source` — default source label

`emit({ name, payload, correlationId, idempotencyKey, version, causationId, sequenceKey, sequenceN, expiresAt, ttlSeconds, depth })`

Path: `POST /api/v1/org/events/ingest/:tenant_id`

## Product guides

See [Integrations](/docs/integrations/overview).

**FAQ** for the Qefro AI Workspace Platform as implemented on app.qefro.com / api.qefro.com.

A scoped AI environment with its own knowledge, instructions, Business Tools, and conversations. See What is an AI Workspace?.</>},

REST for existing HTTPS APIs and OpenAPI specs. Backend SDK for OTP, login, and multi-step workflows. See REST vs SDK.</>},

# Glossary

Source: https://docs.qefro.com/docs/glossary/

> Canonical Qefro terminology aligned with the current architecture, with links to detailed documentation.

This glossary defines canonical Qefro terminology as of October 2026.

| Term | Canonical Definition | Reference |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Organization (Tenant)** | Top-level customer account boundary for data isolation, billing, and global settings. | [Multi-Tenant Architecture](/docs/concepts/multi-tenant-ai-architecture), [Organizations](/docs/platform/organizations) |
| **AI Workspace** | Isolated operational boundary within an organization. Owns dedicated knowledge collections, channels, tools, and app installations. | [What is an AI Workspace?](/docs/concepts/what-is-an-ai-workspace) |
| **Customer AI** | Customer-facing assistants on Website Widget, WhatsApp Cloud API, and Instagram Messaging API. | [Customer vs Employee AI](/docs/concepts/customer-ai-vs-employee-ai), [Customer AI](/docs/platform/customer-ai) |
| **Employee AI** | Employee-facing AI on the branded Internal Portal for operational workflows. | [Employee AI](/docs/platform/employee-ai), [Internal Portal](/docs/platform/internal-portal) |
| **Qefro Runtime** | The unified engine executing conversational chat, Hybrid RAG, FlowRunner, Runtime Actions, and event dispatch. | [Runtime Architecture](/docs/developer/concepts/runtime) |
| **FlowRunner** | The deterministic multi-step state machine orchestrating Business Flows across chat, events, schedules, and webhooks. | [FlowRunner Concepts](/docs/developer/concepts/flows), [Run Business Flows](/docs/guides/run-business-flows) |
| **Runtime Action** | An authorized, auditable operational task executed by Qefro Runtime (e.g. `entity.order.create` or generic HTTP tool). | [Business Actions](/docs/concepts/business-actions) |
| **Action Authority** | The independent runtime security boundary ensuring the model cannot bypass authorization or inject authority parameters. | [AI Agent Security](/docs/concepts/ai-agent-security) |
| **Runtime Adapter** | Internal execution dispatcher routing tool invocations to either native runtime storage (`entity.*`) or external SDK connections. | [Runtime Architecture](/docs/developer/concepts/runtime) |
| **Marketplace App** | A declarative metadata package (`hosting: runtime`) executed natively by Qefro Runtime without an app server. | [Build Your First App](/docs/solutions/build-your-first-app), [Runtime vs SDK](/docs/solutions/runtime-vs-sdk) |
| **Metadata Package** | The bundle of YAML declarations defining a Marketplace App (`manifest.yaml`, `entities/`, `workflows/`, `ui/`, `events/`). | [Marketplace Architecture](/docs/solutions/architecture) |
| **Entity** | A declared business data model (e.g., `reservation.yaml`, `property.yaml`) managed in triple-isolated runtime storage. | [Entity Schema](/docs/solutions/entity-schema) |
| **Installation** | A workspace-specific deployment of a published Marketplace App, keyed by `(tenant_id, workspace_id, installation_id)`. | [Marketplace Installation](/docs/solutions/installation) |
| **SDK Connection** | An HMAC-signed HTTPS webhook connection (`POST /qefro`) connecting external systems of record (ERP/POS/CRM). | [External SDK Connection](/docs/developer/external-sdk-connection), [Backend SDK](/docs/business-tools/backend-sdk) |
| **Customer Hub** | Tenant-wide customer identity and profile platform linking people across channels and apps. | [Customer Hub](/docs/solutions/customer-hub), [People Overview](/docs/user/people/overview) |
| **Person** | A human identity record in the Customer Hub with verified identifiers (`phone`, `email`, `instagram_id`). | [Customer Hub](/docs/solutions/customer-hub) |
| **Customer** | A Person who has an active relationship, account, or transactions with the tenant organization. | [Customer Hub](/docs/solutions/customer-hub) |
| **Business Flow** | A multi-step declarative workflow defined in YAML and executed by FlowRunner. | [Define Business Flows](/docs/guides/define-business-flows) |
| **Business Event** | A standardized event envelope emitted onto the PostgreSQL event bus triggering automations and flows. | [Event-Driven Triggers](/docs/guides/event-driven-triggers), [Event Reference](/docs/reference/event-reference) |
| **Hybrid RAG** | Retrieval system combining dense neural embeddings (Zvec) and sparse lexical search (BM25) with citations. | [Hybrid RAG](/docs/concepts/hybrid-rag) |
| **Website Widget** | Embeddable Customer AI chat interface loaded from CDN and connected to an AI Workspace via WebSocket/HTTP. | [Website Widget](/docs/platform/website-widget) |
| **WhatsApp Channel** | Direct integration with Meta's WhatsApp Cloud API supporting text, audio (STT), flows, and catalog discovery. | [WhatsApp Channel](/docs/platform/whatsapp) |
| **Instagram Channel** | Direct integration with Meta's Instagram Messaging API supporting DMs, quick replies, and private comment replies. | [Instagram Channel](/docs/platform/instagram) |
| **Global Tax Engine** | Platform service calculating transaction, order, and invoice taxes based on configurable country and regional tax rules. | [Tax Engine](/docs/solutions/tax-engine) |

## Terms to Avoid (Deprecated Historical Concepts)

| Deprecated Term | Current Canonical Term | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| `hosting: managed` | `hosting: runtime` | Marketplace Apps are declarative metadata packages; no container or server is hosted. |
| Managed Marketplace App | Metadata Marketplace App | Emphasizes that apps are metadata executed by Qefro Runtime. |
| SDK-hosted Marketplace App | External SDK Connection | The SDK is exclusively for connecting external systems of record, not building marketplace apps. |
| Qefro Studio | Marketplace App Generator (`qefro app init`) | Modern metadata generator replaces legacy studio scaffolding. |
| `/qefro process` for apps | Metadata Runtime Execution | Only external SDK backends expose a `/qefro` webhook; marketplace apps have no `/qefro` process. |
